Reason for (R): the 2009 run's January 1 to 17 tail is supported only by that one year, so it is kept as a one-off in original_dates and not added to the yearly window. The earlier Dec 6 to Jan 17 union was rejected because it adds 17 January days that only one run uses.

problems.issue: Set to yearly_season, but the only dated run is 2010. The row's own open list says 2009 and 2011 are unchecked. My lookups found no Summer Camp evidence for 2009 or 2011 (2011 hits were unrelated: Hall Pass, Trick-or-Treat, Thundercats). A yearly recurrence is not supported by the evidence.
problems.fix: Use one_off_replay for the 2010 run, or keep yearly_season with an explicit flag that it is unconfirmed and admin-gated until a second year is found.

problems.issue: Sept 6, 2010 is reconstructed (R). The reasoning is sound: 13 weeks from June 7 is Sept 6, which is also Labor Day. The (R) marking and reason are present, so this is acceptable but should stay flagged as a reconstruction.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label. Optionally cite the 13-week arithmetic directly.

problems.issue: No existing season is reused. Halloween (Sept 20 to Nov 11) does not overlap June to Sept 6, so there is no conflict. The name is fine.
problems.fix: None required.

problems.issue: Only the 2010 year is dated. The source list is correct: articleId=1780 (Pet Parade Sept 2-3, 2010, 'last Summer Camp event') and TTH 85170 ('13 weeks beginning this week') both check out in lookup. The release date of June 7, 2010 (TTH 86237) also checks out.
problems.fix: None for the 2010 entry. Do not add other years without a source.

problems.issue: Weekly themes have no dates, so there is no slot cadence. The season window alone is wireable, but no weekly schedule exists.
problems.fix: Leave slots null and state that the window is season-only.

critiques.notes: The core 2010 facts hold up under my own lookups: the 13-week run, the June 7 release, and the Sept 2-3 Pet Parade as the last event. The Labor Day end is a reasonable (R) reconstruction. The main calendar error is recurrence: yearly_season is not justified by a single dated year. Wireable as a one-year window with the (R) end, but the recurrence must change before it is treated as a repeating season.

problems.issue: 2010-06-07 is the virtual Summer Camp release date (TTH 86237), but the June 4, 2010 update (articleId=1498) is already centered on Summer Camp with the Greenwood Warpstone and camps. The true first day may be the June 4 update week, not June 7. The row does not explain why the start is the release date rather than the announcement week that TTH 85170 uses for its 13-week count.
problems.fix: Keep 2010-06-07 but note in the source that the start is the release date and that the June 4 update (1498) may mark the season's opening; or mark the start (R) with that reason.

problems.issue: 2010-09-06 is arithmetic (13 weeks from June 7 = Sept 6), marked (R). That is acceptable, but the reason cites Labor Day and 13 weeks as if they were a source. No article gives the end date. Sept 6 also falls after the last dated event (Pet Parade Sept 2-3).
problems.fix: Keep the (R) marking, and state in the row that the end is computed as start + 13 weeks, not sourced.

problems.issue: one_off_replay with season null is consistent with a single dated year, but a one-off window is not a season row, so a builder cannot load it as a scheduled window without a staff decision. Labeled as wireable-ready elsewhere would be inconsistent.
problems.fix: Keep one_off_replay, mark it staff-started, and leave wireable false until staff accept the (R) end date.

problems.issue: Chatty's Greenwood camp is tied to the 2010 virtual event by weekly community-team language and dates, not by an explicit name match. The row states the Summer Camp quests and places as fact.
problems.fix: Keep the open note, and label the Chatty/Robbie camp links as an inferred tie in the evidence section.

problems.issue: Marshmallow pet (wiki: Pet Pals) and the reward claims have no price, currency or date, and the wiki cite is not a dated source. The Pirates Plunder claim cites a wiki page for a themed week that the articles only mention.
problems.fix: Keep as open; do not treat the reward as a dated fact.

critiques.notes: Dates check out against the sources I could see: TTH 86237 gives a June 7, 2010 release, TTH 85170 gives 13 weeks, and articleId 1780 gives Pet Parade Sept 2-3 as the last Summer Camp event. The 2010-only finding is honest: searches found no 2009 or 2011 run. Zones, NPCs and quest titles are sourced. Main weaknesses are the start-date choice (release vs June 4 update) and the reconstructed end date, which is correctly marked (R). The season row should stay null until staff accept a one-time window.

problems.issue: Season is null, yet the row has a dated 2010 window (2010-06-07 to 2010-09-06) and says a one-time window should be replayed. A builder cannot load it: there is no season window and no slot cadence.
problems.fix: Either add a season row named 'Summer Camp' with start 06-07 and end 09-06 marked (R) with reason 'Labor Day, 13 weeks from June 7', or state explicitly that the event is staff-started and give the window fields in a structured form. Do not leave the window only in prose.

problems.issue: 'one_off_replay' is not a clear cadence for a community season. The row also says 'staff-started or one-time window' without choosing one. The text and the field disagree about whether a window is created.
problems.fix: Pick one value. For a Community Team season with a single dated year and no second year found, use admin_only (staff start each summer) and say so. Do not describe a window that is not in the season field.

problems.issue: The source is a long prose string mixing citations and the (R) reason. The start date is also not explained: the June 4, 2010 update (articleId=1498) was 'centered on Summer Camp', so a June 4 start is possible. The June 7 date is the virtual release, not confirmed as the first themed week.
problems.fix: Split sources into fields (start_source, end_source). Note that the start is the June 7 release and that June 4 (articleId=1498) may be the announcement week. Keep the (R) reason on the end date only.

problems.issue: 2010-09-06 is reconstructed from 13 weeks plus Labor Day. The arithmetic checks: June 7 plus 13 weeks lands on Sept 6, 2010. The reconstruction is valid but must stay marked (R).
problems.fix: Keep (R). No change needed beyond structuring the source.

problems.fix: Cite the 1510 summary wording as the basis for the tie. Keep the assumption flagged.

problems.issue: No overlap with Halloween (Sep 20 to Nov 11). The June to early September window does not swallow unrelated months. No reuse of an existing season name is needed.

critiques.notes: Dates verified against the lookup: the virtual Summer Camp release on June 7, 2010 (tentonhammer 86237), 13 weeks from the announcement week (85170), 14 camp land quests, the June 4 update (articleId=1498), and the Pet Parade on Sept 2-3 as the last event (articleId=1780). No 2009 or 2011 Summer Camp evidence was found in articles or wiki, so a single dated year is correct and yearly recurrence is not supported. The 2010 window is evidenced; the end date is reconstructed. The row is true as far as it goes, but it is not wireable until a season window or slot cadence is written into the structured fields.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks out. problems.issue: The end date 2010-09-05 is derived as '13 weeks from Monday 2010-06-07'. But the cited source (tentonhammer node 85170) says the events run 13 weeks 'beginning this week', i.e. from the announcement week, not from the June 7 live date. The pack itself says the announcement week is the June 4 week (a Friday, so its Monday is May 31). Counting 13 weeks from May 31 gives an end of 2010-08-29, not 2010-09-05. The row picks the start that fits its end and does not flag the conflict. The Labor Day cross-check (article 1510, undated) only supports an end near Sept 5-6.
problems.fix: Keep the start 2010-06-07 (quoted, node 86237). Mark the end as a (R) range, for example 2010-08-29 to 2010-09-05, with the reason: 13 weeks from the announcement week (node 85170) versus 'through Labor Day' (article 1510). Pick one end for the scheduler and say which source it follows, or leave the end open.

problems.issue: The claim 'themed events run 13 weeks beginning the week of the announcement' is paraphrased as a June 7 start in the derivation. The row mixes the announcement week with the live date without saying so.
problems.fix: State the two anchors separately: announcement week (June 2010, undated week start) and live release June 7 (quoted). Do not call the 13-week end derived from June 7.

problems.issue: The season window is the 2010 run only, and the source is marked (R). This is acceptable as a one-off window, and 'Summer Camp' does not clash with the existing Halloween season. critiques.notes: Verified via lookup: node 86237 quotes 'released its virtual Summer Camp on June 7 (2010)' and article 1510 says themed events ran weekly 'through Labor Day' with a new Activity Calendar each week. Node 85170 says '13 weeks beginning this week'. The start of 2010-06-07 is sourced. The end is the weak point: it is arithmetic on a start the source does not state, and it conflicts with the source's own 'this week' anchor (about a week earlier). Zones, NPCs and the quest titles were not re-checked in full in this lens; they match the pack's listed locale ids and the id check is clean. Wireable is true for the 2010 window with the end marked as a range, but the pass is withheld until the end is fixed.

problems.issue: The end date 2010-09-05 is derived, not quoted. I checked the arithmetic: Mon 2010-06-07 is a Monday, +91 days is Mon 2010-09-06, so the 13th week ends Sun 2010-09-05. Labor Day 2010 was Mon 2010-09-06, so the cross-check holds. But node 85170 says '13 weeks beginning this week' from the announcement week (about May 31 to June 6), which gives Sun 2010-08-29. The row flags this and keeps 09-05. That is acceptable as a derived window, but the lead should confirm it before loading.
problems.fix: Keep 2010-09-05 with the (R) tag, or set the end to 2010-08-29 if the lead prefers the announcement-week anchor. Record the alternative in the source text, as the row already does.

problems.issue: one_off_replay is sensible. The only evidence is the 2010 run, and nothing I checked (articles 1510, 85170, 1593) names a later year. The Spanish article 1593 (Fashion Week) is undated, so it cannot support a yearly season.
problems.fix: Keep one_off_replay. Do not add a yearly recurrence unless a dated later-year source is found.

problems.issue: Article 1593 (Spanish, Fashion Week) gives expected in-game event times on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. The row says no clock times are sourced, and that is true for the English sources, but 1593 is a time source the row does not mention. Its year is also unknown.
problems.fix: Add 1593 to open as an unverified candidate for weekly slots. Do not use its times until its year and the 2010 link are confirmed.

problems.issue: No overlap with the existing Halloween season (9/20 to 11/11). The name 'Summer Camp' is new and does not clash with any defined season, so no reuse is needed.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: June 7 2010 is a Monday, 13 weeks is 91 days, Labor Day 2010 is Sept 6, and the 2010-06-04 patch note is correctly treated as a pre-launch announcement, not a run date. The season window covers the June to early September run and does not swallow Halloween. The window is wireable as a 2010 season with the derived end flagged. Not a verified yearly pattern.

problems.issue: The 2010-09-05 end is derived, not quoted. The only direct anchor (tentonhammer node 85170, '13 weeks beginning this week') points to the announcement week, which is the June 4 update (articles 1498/1502), so it gives about 2010-08-29. The 09-05 choice rests on an undated 'through Labor Day' line in article 1510. Labor Day 2010 was 2010-09-06, so the cross-check is arithmetically right but weak. Article 1780 (Pet Parade, 'last Summer Camp event') is reported elsewhere in the packs as Sept 2-3, 2010, which the answer does not weigh.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label, but state the reason for choosing 09-05 over 08-29 (Pet Parade Sept 2-3 as the last event, if verified from article 1780), or use the announcement-week anchor and say so. Either way, record both candidate ends in the open list.

problems.issue: Start date and the 13-week quotes check out in the facts corpus (node 86237 'June 7th'; node 85170 'will run for 13 weeks beginning this week'). problems.issue: The fixed 17-22 Feb window is fitted to the two observed years (2011, 2012) and does not follow the rule the runs actually share. Both runs were Friday through the Monday of Presidents' Day (2011: Fri 18 to Mon 21; 2012: Fri 17 to Mon 20), and Presidents' Day is the third Monday of February, which falls between 15 and 21 Feb. In years where it falls on 15 or 16 Feb (e.g. 2010, 2015), the Friday-to-Monday run starts on 12 or 13 Feb and lies outside 17-22 Feb. In 2013 (Mon 18 Feb) only part of the run overlaps. The window therefore misses the typical run in some years while being correct for the two evidenced ones.

Keep the 2011 and 2012 original_dates as the evidenced checks. Mark the rule as (R) with the reason that it is inferred from two years. season.name: Thanksgiving Turkey Dance
season.source: (R) Window reconstructed, not sourced. US Thanksgiving is the 4th Thursday of November (22 to 28 Nov). The window runs from 22 Nov to 29 Nov so it covers the Thursday and the Friday after it in every year: the Friday after falls on 23 to 29 Nov. The end was widened from 28 to 29 Nov because when Thanksgiving is Thu 28 Nov the Friday is 29 Nov. The Friday-after rule comes from article 645 (http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=645), whose year is not in the pack. The 2010 run (Thu 25 and Fri 26 Nov) is inside the window. No existing season matches; Halloween is a different event.

problems.fix: Set end_month 11, end_day 29 (or compute the window from the 4th Thursday of November plus one day each year). Rewrite the (R) reason to say it spans the Thursday to the Friday after US Thanksgiving, with the year-by-year rule.

open: Start and end days are not in any source; Feb 1 to Mar 31 is reconstructed (R) from the wiki's month range. Verify against a dated start/end before the calendar goes live.

problems.issue: Feb 1 to Mar 31 is reconstructed. The wiki pages (Festival of Hearts, Events) say only 'held from February through March', and Merry Vale says 'During February'. The (R) marker is present, but the reason is thin: the wiki month range is the only support for the day numbers.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) flag. Add the reason that the window is the wiki's month range widened to whole months, and that the 2010 (Feb 12) and 2012 (Feb 7) dated starts fall inside it.

problems.issue: Null, but the evidence cites locale:4452 and 1415 for the name and 'has begun' text. The exact announce string 'The annual Festival of Hearts has begun in Merry Vale.' comes from article 969 (fact list), not the locale table.
problems.fix: Cite article 969 for the announce text, or set locale_id to the matching string if one is found.

problems.issue: The 'annual' recurrence rests on the wiki's 'annual' wording. The only dated occurrences are 2010 and 2012, and the 2016+ articles are unchecked. The claim is adequately sourced for a yearly season but is not confirmed by a third dated year.
problems.fix: Note in open that recurrence is supported by wiki text plus two dated years, not by a dated 2014 or later run.

problems.issue: 'Every day' cadence is taken from locale text with no clock time. Acceptable because no slots are set and the open list says so, but the row says the activities run daily without a source for daily cadence beyond the text.

critiques.notes: Core facts check out: article 967 dates the live start to the February 12, 2010 update in Merry Vale; the wiki Template:News/Archive has the February 7, 2012 Merry Vale festival update; the wiki Festival of Hearts, Events and Merry Vale pages all give the February-through-March month range. Zone is consistently Merry Vale for the English sources, and the French and Spanish zone conflicts are correctly left open. Original dates agree with each other and with the season window, which covers both. No season name collides with the existing Halloween window. Wireable as a yearly Feb 1 to Mar 31 season window with the (R) flag, but the day range should not be treated as confirmed.

problems.issue: Feb 1 to Mar 31 is a reconstruction. The wiki (Festival of Hearts, Events, Merry Vale) says only 'held from February through March' and Cudip's page says 'annually each February'. Taking all of March can run about a month past a real end date, and no source gives a day. The (R) label and reason are present, so this is acceptable, but the end day is a guess.
problems.fix: Keep (R) on the season. Narrow end to the first half of March, or leave the window as Feb 1 to Mar 31 and flag it in the scheduler as reconstructed until a dated end is found.

problems.issue: Only two dated years (2010-02-12 and 2012-02-07). Both fall inside the window, which is consistent. 'annual' is supported by wiki text, not by dated occurrences, and the 2016 and later articles were not checked.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season. Add later dated occurrences (articles 2016, 2018, 2019, 2500, 2501) before treating the window as confirmed across years.

problems.issue: Announce text 'has begun' is taken from article 969 and is not tied to a locale id (null). Not a calendar error, but the row cannot be checked against client text.
problems.fix: Link the locale id if one matches 'has begun in Merry Vale', or mark the announce as article-sourced.

problems.issue: No conflict. Halloween (Sep 20 to Nov 11) does not overlap Feb to Mar. The name is new, which is correct since no existing season covers it.

critiques.notes: Sources checked in the lookup: wiki Festival of Hearts, Events, Merry Vale and Cudip say February through March, annual; article 967 says live from the February 12, 2010 update; Template:News/Archive has the February 7, 2012 update. The yearly_season recurrence fits a holiday with no slots. Season window is wireable because it is sourced at month level and the (R) reason is stated, but the day-level edges are reconstructed. Activities have no clock times and correctly have no slots.

critiques.notes: The row is honest. It gives no dates, zones or cadence, and it does not invent a clock time or a season, and the confidence of 0.15 fits. The window itself rests on the wiki line 'throughout the month of April', which is a single page statement, not a run record.

problems.issue: 'yearly_season' is sensible for a seasonal anniversary event, and the wiki ns14 and ns0 pages both describe it as annual. Calendar fit is fine: no overlap with the Halloween window (Sep 20 to Nov 11), and no existing season is reused under the same name.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: the April 1 to April 30 window is supported by wiki ns0 Events ('throughout the month of April') and ns14 (seasonal around the April 29 anniversary). The 2013 blog (ns500) is dated April 29, 2013, which agrees with the anniversary framing but gives no run end. The 2012 end date May 24 is confirmed by article 2580 (articles index). The season is wireable as a yearly April window with a 2012 end-only override. The row fails on original_dates: the 2013 entry is not a run, and the 2012 start is missing. The Birthday Cake Hat citation also needs correcting. Summer Splash is correctly left out of the dated record.

problems.issue: Sacred Grove is listed as an event zone, but locale:707 only says the top-rated chefs are from Sacred Grove. problems.issue: The April 1 to April 30 window is sourced to wiki ns0 'throughout the month of April' (verified). It is correctly marked (R) with a reason, and the 2012 May 24 tail is kept as an override. This holds.

critiques.notes: Verified: wiki ns0 Events and ns14 Category:Birthday Bash Weapons say annual, throughout April, around the April 29 launch (anniversary framing). Article 2580 is verified: third-anniversary Birthday Bash ran through May 24, 2012, with Queen Valerian's Sanctuary cake bake-off, daily party-prep quests and Cakenstein. Wiki ns0 Birthday Cake Hat is verified as an unobtainable item given to everyone who logged in during 2012 Birthday Bash, so the corrected citation is right. Locale 6792 supports the Balloon Bow encounter. Summer Splash (19967/19968) and the undated texts are correctly excluded. Halloween (Sep 20 to Nov 11) does not overlap the April window. problems.issue: The April 1 to April 30 window is a month-level reconstruction, and it misses every dated run end the sources give. critiques.notes: Lookup confirms the core dates: 1261 and 1267 for 2010 (party to May 10, anniversary Apr 29, eight zones named in 1267), 2099 and 2107 for 2011 (to May 18, anniversary Apr 28), and 2580 for 2012 (through May 24). problems.issue: The window is justified as covering 2010 to 2012. critiques.notes: The calendar logic is sound. problems.issue: The 2011 end date May 18 rests on articles 2107 and 2099 (summary-level, not re-run here). The 2012 end May 24 is confirmed by lookup (article 2580: 'ran through May 24, 2012'), and I confirmed it. The 2010 end May 10 is confirmed by 1267 ('until May 10, 2010').

critiques.notes: Checked by lookup: article 1267 states the 2010 party ran from the posting day to May 10 with eight zones (names match the answer exactly); article 2580 states the 2012 party ran through May 24; wiki Camellia says she is the royal party planner in Sanctuary during the Birthday Bash. The anniversary-date conflict (April 28 vs April 29) is recorded per year and left open, which is correct. The season window Apr 28 to May 24 covers the 2010-2012 runs and does not overlap Halloween. problems.issue: Cakenstein location conflict and bake-off host conflict are correctly kept open. The 2010 Cakenstein boss fights are in the open list but the cited article 1282 summary is not confirmed by the articles I found (the Cakenstein boss battle is in articles.json:21096).
problems.fix: Cite articles.json:21096 for the 2010 Cakenstein boss battle and the 2010 party areas across eight zones.

critiques.notes: The main claims check out: May 24, 2012 end (articles.json:18884; facts 23993; locale:695 'Birthday Bash 2012 marks the 3rd Anniversary'); April 29, 2013 (articles.json:20844); Flitter invitation text (locale:4952) and bake-off (locale:707) exist. 'Making this Birthday Bash a Summer Splash' is at locale 2642737684 (out of the pack's citation). The season window is wireable as a yearly season (Apr 29 to May 24), but the row misstates 2010 as undated, which understates the evidence. Kind 'holiday' with recurrence yearly_season is sensible.

problems.issue: The April 29 start is not sourced for the Bash in any year. It is the anniversary date from article 2924, which is known only from its summary, not a dated fetch. The 2012 Bash announcement (articleId=2580) is dated 2012-04-26 in schedule-packs, so the Bash was already live before April 29 that year. A pack note also says the anniversary recurs on April 28. The start is therefore likely wrong or at least unverified.
problems.fix: Mark the start as unknown and do not set a fixed start. Either use the 2012 announcement date (about April 26) as the earliest observed date, with a (R) reason, or leave the window open until a 2010 or 2011 start is found.

problems.issue: The window joins a 2013 start (April 29) to a 2012 end (May 24). Those are different years, so the span is not a sourced run for any single year. The wiki's 'throughout April' wording conflicts with the May 24 end and is left open.
problems.fix: Record each year's observed start and end separately in original_dates, and do not build one yearly window from mixed years until the run length is sourced.

problems.issue: yearly_season is a sensible kind of recurrence for an anniversary holiday. The row itself says the window should not be enabled, so it is not yet a usable recurrence.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season for the holiday, but set the window to disabled or admin_only until the start and end are sourced for at least one year.

problems.issue: Both years have null dates. The 2010 anniversary has an undated article (1282), and 2011 relies on wiki item pages that give no dates. These years add no calendar evidence.
problems.fix: Keep them as attested-but-undated entries and do not use them to fix the window.

problems.issue: The source string says a 2013 start and a 2012 end are the basis for the window, but the 2013 start rests on a summary-only article, which the row does not mark.
problems.fix: Add the (R) reason that the 2013 date is from article summary only, not a dated fetch.

critiques.notes: The row is honest: it marks the window as reconstructed (R), leaves 2010 and 2011 undated, and keeps the Summer Splash link out. Its calendar claim still fails because the start date is not supported and the 2012 announcement date (April 26) contradicts the April 29 start. The season name 'Birthday Bash' does not clash with Halloween, and the yearly holiday kind fits. Not wireable until a start is sourced for a single year.

problems.issue: The 2010 and 2011 entries are marked null/undated, but articles.json has sourced end dates the pack missed. The 1st-anniversary article summaries say the party ran from the launch-day kickoff (about April 29) until May 10, 2010. The 2nd-birthday post (captured 2011-04-30, dates inferred) says the party ran until May 18, 2011. The 2012 press release (April 30 post) and article 2580 both give May 24, 2012.
problems.fix: Set 2010 end to 2010-05-10 and 2011 end to 2011-05-18, each with its article as source. Mark the start as the anniversary kickoff (R) with the reason. Replace the statement that 2010 is undated.

problems.issue: The window April 29 - May 24 is built from the 2012 end only. The 2010 and 2011 ends (May 10, May 18) fall well inside it, so the window is longer than most years and its end is not stable across years. The reconstruction is flagged (R), which is right, but the evidence is weaker than the pack claims.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) flag and state that the end varies: May 10 (2010), May 18 (2011), May 24 (2012). Either widen the stated range to cover the typical run or leave the season disabled until the start is confirmed.

problems.issue: The wiki 'throughout April' conflict is listed as unresolved, but the anniversary-kickoff wording in the 2010 summaries supports an April 29 start. The start is still inferred, not stated as a date in any source.
problems.fix: Record the 2010 kickoff-day wording as supporting evidence for April 29 and say the exact start is inferred, so the start is not presented as sourced.

problems.issue: The pack says Queen Valerian ran the 2012 bake-off, and Camellia hosted it in 2010. Both are sourced as stated, but the pack's cake-bake claim for 2010 cites locale:707 as the only source. That is acceptable, but the conflict stays open and should not be stated as one fact.
problems.fix: Keep both hosts tagged by year (Camellia 2010, Queen Valerian 2012) and do not merge them.

critiques.notes: The row is mostly true as far as it goes. Sourced: the 2012 end on May 24 (article 2580), the 2013 4th birthday on April 29 with the Sanctuary Bash area (article 2924), and the 2011 Bash items (wiki). The pack's 2010 'undated' claim is partly wrong: article summaries in articles.json give a May 10, 2010 end and a 2011 May 18 end, and the pack did not use them. The start date is still inferred, so wireable is false until the start is sourced for at least one year. No cadence or clock time is invented, and slots and weekly are correctly null. Revival recurrence as yearly_season is sensible, but the season should stay disabled until the window is settled.

problems.issue: The April 29 start is the anniversary date, not a sourced start of the Bash. No source gives a Bash start in any year (article 2580 says only 'ran through May 24, 2012'; article 2924 says the 4th birthday was April 29 with a Bash area in Sanctuary). The window is reconstructed, and the wiki 'throughout April' wording conflicts with it.
problems.fix: Keep the season marked (R) with the reason in the source field, and do not enable it in the scheduler until a 2010, 2011 or 2013 start or end is sourced and the April conflict is resolved.

problems.issue: Recorded as a 'start' of 2013-04-29, but article 2924 only says the 4th birthday fell on April 29 and the Bash area existed. It does not say the Bash began that day.
problems.fix: Record 2013 as an anniversary date (April 29) with no Bash start, or mark the start as (R).

problems.issue: No year has both a sourced start and end. 2010 and 2011 are null, 2012 has an end only, and 2013 has a start only, so the years cannot confirm each other's window length.
problems.fix: State in the notes that the window length is unconfirmed; do not present the April 29 to May 24 span as a verified yearly run.

problems.issue: yearly_season is a reasonable kind of recurrence for an anniversary-tied event, and the row correctly declines to set slots or weekly. The recurrence is only as good as the unresolved window.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season, but set the window to unconfirmed and not wireable until the open items are closed.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: no name clash (Halloween is the only existing season, and 'Birthday Bash' does not reuse it). The window of about 26 days does not swallow unrelated months, and the 2012 May 24 end and 2013 April 29 anniversary are both in the articles (2580, 2924). The row is honest about its reconstruction and open items, so it passes as far as it goes. Confirmed in the articles: 2580 says the Bash 'runs through May 24, 2012'; 2924 says the 4th birthday was April 29, 2013; 1282 is undated (its summary puts it around spring 2010). Not wireable because the season start is an inference from the anniversary, not a sourced Bash start.

original_dates.source: articles: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=106 (announcement: 'concert by The Dares on the Snowhill stage ... June 2 at 4pm Pacific'); wiki page The Dares: players on server 1 at 4pm Pacific saw the E3 performance live at Snowhill's stage. Announcement gives the plan; the wiki confirms the live run. (R) end date null: no run length in sources.

activities: Live concert streamed from E3 (The Dares performing the Free Realms theme song 'It's Your World')

announce.text: Experience the music of Free Realms in a concert on the Snowhill stage June 2nd, 4:00 pm Pacific.

revival.why: The source is a single dated E3 2009 live concert, not a yearly holiday or a repeating activity. No season window or clock cadence is evidenced. Replaying it, if wanted, should be an admin-started run at the original time. A second undated Dares concert (locale:406760) is not dated, so no recurrence is recorded.

evidence.claim: The Dares performed a live concert on the Snowhill stage, streamed from E3, on June 2 at 4pm Pacific (2009).
evidence.source: articles: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=106 (fact: 'performed a live concert on the Snowhill stage ... on June 2 at 4pm Pacific'); wiki page The Dares (players at 4pm Pacific on server 1)

evidence.claim: The concert was tied to a Guinness World Record for the first concert held simultaneously in the real world and a virtual space.
evidence.source: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=132 and http://www.tentonhammer.com:80/node/69709 (per prior pass; not re-verified in this pass)

evidence.claim: The theme song 'It's Your World' was performed at the concert.
evidence.source: articles: article 106 summary says The Dares were to perform the theme song; article 132 per prior pass (undated)

open: Article 132 is undated; its date (roughly late June 2009 per the summary) is not confirmed, so the 2009-06-02 date rests on article 106's announcement.
Guinness record and theme-song performance are cited to article 132 and tentonhammer, which I did not re-read in this pass.
No run end time or duration is sourced, so end is null.

Milk Rocks (Sanctuary), Milk Carton, Spring Concert '09 T-Shirt and the Dares client kit (Boombox, Dares Teleport Ben/Martin/Matt, Dares End Fireworks, Dares Event Controller) are excluded as unconfirmed. They need their own checks before any merge.
Second Dares concert (locale:406760, Freewheelers security) is undated; it may be a separate event.
No NPCs or in-game activities are confirmed for this event; no season or slot cadence exists.
Halloween season is unrelated to this event; it is not reused.

problems.issue: Article 106 is cited as proof the concert was performed, but it is a pre-launch 'What is New' announcement ('will be', 'were to perform'). The lookup extract reads in the past tense, but the announcement cannot confirm the live run. The wiki page 'The Dares' is the only source that says players saw the E3 performance live at 4pm Pacific on server 1.
problems.fix: Keep article 106 as the source for the planned date and time. State that the live run is confirmed by the wiki page 'The Dares' (server 1, 4pm Pacific) and article 132 (Guinness record), and do not cite 106 for past tense.

problems.issue: The year 2009 rests on the wiki page title slug ('2009-free-realms-and-the-dares-set-world-record-concert') and the E3 link, not on a dated sentence. This is reasonable but should be named as such.
problems.fix: Cite the wiki page title and the E3 2009 context explicitly as the year source.

problems.issue: The 4:00 pm Pacific time is an announced plan. Only the wiki's 'players ... at 4pm Pacific' supports it as the run time. This is sourced, not invented, so it is acceptable, but the row should not treat it as a verified broadcast time.
problems.fix: Label the time as the announced and observed start time, with the source for each.

critiques.notes: The core date (2009-06-02, Snowhill stage, 4pm Pacific, E3 live stream) is supported by article 106 and the wiki page 'The Dares'. The Guinness record is confirmed by the lookup of article 132. The theme-song claim is only supported via article 132's summary and was not re-read in full. Open items are correctly listed: no end time, no NPCs, no activities, and the undated client kit and second concert are excluded. Halloween is not reused, which is correct. The row is a valid one-off with a dated source and can be wired as a single occurrence with end null and admin replay only.

problems.issue: The 4:00 pm Pacific clock time appears only in the announce text and the source notes. It has no structured field, so a builder cannot tell the run's start time or time zone from the row itself.
problems.fix: Add a start_time of 16:00 with time_zone America/Los_Angeles (source: article 106 fact 'June 2 at 4pm Pacific'; wiki The Dares 'server 1 at 4pm Pacific').

problems.issue: The source text for the 2009-06-02 date rests on article 106, which is a pre-launch 'What is New' announcement ('were to perform'). The live occurrence is confirmed only by the wiki and the undated article 132. The row presents the plan date as settled without marking it as a plan.
problems.fix: Mark the date as an announced date with a confirmed-run note, e.g. '(R) announced 2009-06-02; live run confirmed by wiki The Dares', so the calendar records what is known.

problems.issue: 'one_off_replay' is not a value a scheduler would normally recognise. A one-off with an admin-started replay is fine for the calendar, but the value needs a schema-defined name.
problems.fix: Use the schema's one-off value (for example 'one_off' with admin_only replay) and keep the replay note in why.

problems.issue: Correctly null. The event is a single dated concert, not a season. The Halloween window does not overlap June, so it is not reused.
problems.fix: None needed.

problems.issue: Null end is acceptable since no run length is sourced, but a one-off concert with a null end leaves the scheduler to guess the duration.
problems.fix: Set a provisional duration marked (R) with reason, or leave null and state that the scheduler should treat it as an instant event.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: the only year is 2009, and the date agrees across article 106 (facts.json 'June 2 at 4pm Pacific'), the wiki page The Dares and the announce text. No second dated occurrence exists, and the undated locale:406760 concert is correctly kept out of the calendar. Article 132 is undated, so it cannot test the year-by-year agreement. The row is true as far as it goes. It is wireable as a single dated one-off, provided the 16:00 Pacific time is made structured.

original_dates.source: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=137 (fact:event 'began July 2, 2009'); end date not stated in any source

props_or_areas: Seaside inn area (celebrants near the inn, article 137)
activities: Complete Seaside quests to earn Seaside Stickers (article 136)
Trade ten Seaside Stickers to Sizzlebottom for a Gold Pinwheel firework (locale:400744, locale:400742)
Grekel card duel Matching Wits (locale:400812, locale:400852)
Cook-off (locale:400900; quest title unconfirmed)
rewards: Seaside Sticker
Gold Pinwheel Firework (locale:395520)
Blue Pinwheel Firework (locale:395521; event tie moderate)
Star Shot Candle (article 136; wiki Star Shot Candle)
Sand Castle, Hula Outfit, Ducky Floaty, Uncle Sam Outfit (Marketplace, article 137)

revival.why: Only one year (2009) is evidenced, with a July 2 start and no end date and no source saying it recurs. A yearly season window cannot be sourced without inventing dates, and a daily/slot cadence has no evidence. Run it as a replay of the 2009 event, not as a yearly season, unless a later year is found.

evidence.claim: Holiday event began July 2, 2009, kicked off by Robgoblin Sizzlebottom near the Seaside inn.
Quests in Seaside earn Seaside Stickers, redeemable for special fireworks, wearables and other items.
Sizzlebottom, Tarisa Teaspoon, Heddy Heathcliff, Shelly Sandishoes and Grekel are the celebrants offering challenges near the Seaside inn.
Sand Castle, Hula Outfit, Ducky Floaty, Uncle Sam Outfit added to Marketplace for the celebration.
Star Shot Candle was formerly acquired via quest Cook-off Catastrophe during the 2009 Seaside Summer Splash.
evidence.source: wiki ns0 'Star Shot Candle' (wiki only; not a client title match)

evidence.claim: Grekel's duel dialog names the Seaside Summer Splash.
Cook-off winner reward text names the Seaside Summer Splash cook-off.

open: No end date for 2009 in any source; no season window written. If Bryce wants a season row, the window would be reconstructed (R) as July 2 to a chosen end date, which needs a source before use. Seasons already defined only include Halloween, so no name reuse applies.
No evidence of any later year; recurrence is one_off_replay, not yearly.
Star Shot Candle acquisition conflict remains: article 136 (Grekel duel) vs wiki (Cook-off Catastrophe). Cook-off Catastrophe has no client title match.
Cook-off quest title is unconfirmed; 'Cook-off Contest' is OCR-only (video w-9vtebjou4/00074).
Blue Pinwheel Firework may be a general firework.
Tarisa Teaspoon (article) vs 'Teaspoon Tarlo' (OCR) not reconciled.
Summer Sparkler Bundle (article 136 claim deadline 7/12/2009) excluded; may be a separate promotion. Articles 2153 and 2160 unchecked.
No prices or currencies attested; marketplace items have null price.

problems.issue: The Grekel-duel acquisition for Star Shot Candle rests on article 136 as cited in the pack, and I could only confirm the wiki version (Cook-off Catastrophe). The two paths conflict and the answer still lists the duel as the source in evidence without reconciling it.
problems.fix: Keep the candle as a reward with both paths marked as conflicting, or drop the acquisition sentence until article 136 text is re-read and quoted.

problems.issue: Cook-off is listed as an activity on the strength of locale:400900, which is a quest_reward label and names no quest title. The title is only OCR-sourced ('Cook-off Contest').
problems.fix: Keep the flag as it is, and state in the activity line that it is a reward-label tie only.

problems.issue: Listed as an event reward although the event tie is only moderate (quest title locale:400772 plus article 137), and the item may be a general firework.
problems.fix: Mark it as 'event tie unverified' in the rewards line itself, not only in open.

problems.issue: Only the 2009 start (July 2) is attested, from article 137, and no end date is sourced. This is correctly marked open, and no season window is invented.
problems.fix: None needed for evidence. A season row would need a reconstructed (R) window with a reason before use.

critiques.notes: I checked the core evidence. Article 137 (July 2, 2009 start, celebrants, Sizzlebottom pinwheels, marketplace items) and article 136 (Seaside Stickers) both appear in the lookup. locale:400812 names the Seaside Summer Splash and locale:400900 names the cook-off reward. Locale 399659 and 19968 confirm that bare 'Summer Splash' is ambiguous, so the alias was correctly dropped. The wiki Star Shot Candle page matches the pack. No clock times or cadences are invented. The row is true as far as it goes; it is not wireable because the only window is an unsourced one-off with no end date and no slot cadence.

problems.issue: End is null. The only dated fact is the 2009-07-02 start from article 137. Article 136 gives a 7/12/2009 claim deadline, but that is for the Summer Sparkler Bundle and is not an event end date. No source supports an end.
problems.fix: Keep end null. If Bryce needs a bounded run, mark it (R) with the reason and cite the 7/12/2009 deadline as a non-end hint, or leave the replay open-ended.

problems.issue: No season window is written. The row correctly says no yearly window can be sourced, and the Halloween season does not clash with a July event, so no name reuse applies.
problems.fix: Leave season null. Do not create a yearly window from one year of evidence.

problems.issue: one_off_replay fits a single-year holiday with no evidence of recurrence. The why field is accurate.
problems.fix: No change needed.

problems.issue: A season row needs a sourced window and a slot cadence needs a sourced schedule. Neither exists: there is one start date and no end.
problems.fix: Keep wireable false until an end date or a second year is sourced. A builder could load the single start date as a dated replay with an open end, but that is not a season window.

critiques.notes: I checked the articles 136 and 137 facts and the wiki Star Shot Candle text. All of them say the event began 2 July 2009 and ran in 2009, and none gives a later year. The calendar fields agree with each other, and the open list records the missing end date and the lack of recurrence. Item and quest issues are outside this lens.

event.name: Summer Camp (virtual summer community event series)

original_dates.source: Start: release date June 7, 2010 per http://tentonhammer.com/node/86237 (the event answer also places the week of the announcement in early June, http://www.tentonhammer.com:80/node/85170). End: last named event Pet Parade, Sept 2-3, 2010, confirmed in http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=1780 which says it was the last Summer Camp event (end day = Sept 3 is the last event day, (R) the exact closing date is not stated).

zones: Greenwood Forest (Chatty's camp, reached by a newly activated Warpstone)
Robbie's rival camp across the lake from Chatty's
Crossroads and the area near the Sanctuary warpstone (Pet Parade route, Server 1)

npcs: Jojo (chugawug, at Summer Camp per locale:441709, 441715)
activities: Weekly themed events (Fashion Week, Sports Week, Arts and Crafts Week, Treasure Hunting Week)
Team competition between Chatty's and Robbie's camps
Pet Parade, Sept 2-3 2010 (article 1780)
Printable weekly Summer Camp Activity Calendar
rewards: Marshmallow pet (wiki 'Pet Pals', available only during Summer Camp; price unsourced)
Camp marketplace and Coin Shop items, housing items (article 1498)

revival.why: Only one dated run (June-Sept 2010) is sourced and the articles call it the last Summer Camp; no second year or fixed cadence exists, so it is not a yearly season or daily slot. Replay only on admin start if staff want it.

evidence.claim: Virtual Summer Camp released June 7, 2010
13 weeks of themed events beginning the week of the announcement; 14 camp land quests
Pet Parade on Server 1, Sept 2 and 3, 2010, described as the last Summer Camp event
Quest titles Chatty's / Robbie's Summer Camp Party
Jojo quest text places Jojo at Summer Camp near Greenwood Forest; the Jojo's Mojo/Dojo/Ninjato set is also filed as SGRevamp Wilds South, so it is not counted as an event quest
Summer Camp is also a permanent place name
Marshmallow pet only during Summer Camp

open: Start day June 7 is the release date; the first themed week may have started a few days different. Not verified against a dated start article.
End date Sept 3 is the last named event day, not a stated closing date.

Season not created: one run only, so no yearly window is evidenced. Creating a Summer Camp season (e.g. June 7 - Sept 3) would be a reconstruction (R) and should be added only if staff want yearly replays.
Summer Camp place name (locale:442124) vs. the 2010 event may be separate; do not merge without a check.
The 14 camp land quests are not titled in any source; only the two party quests are listed.
Marshmallow price and names of June 2010 camp items are unsourced.
Pirate Week is not tied to Summer Camp and is excluded.

problems.issue: 2010-06-07 is the release date from tentonhammer node/86237 (confirmed: 'released its virtual Summer Camp on June 7'). It is not a sourced start of the first themed week, and the row's own open list says so. Labelling it as the start of the run overstates it.
problems.fix: Keep the value but mark it '(release date, not first-week start)' in the source field, or add an (R) tag on the start.

problems.issue: 2010-09-03 is inferred. Article 1780 (confirmed this pass) says the Pet Parade was on Server 1 on Sept 2 and 3, 2010 and was the last Summer Camp event, but gives no closing date.
problems.fix: Keep the end as '(R)' with the reason already given; it is the last named event day, not a stated end.

problems.issue: The claim that the event ran 13 weeks starting the announcement week, with 14 camp land quests, cites node/85170. My lookup of articles for that wording returned nothing, so I could not re-verify it. It is not needed for the dates, but it is the only support for the run length.
problems.fix: Re-check node/85170 directly, or drop the 13-week claim from the calendar basis.

problems.issue: season is null and recurrence is one_off_replay. This is consistent with one dated run and no second year, so it is not a calendar error. But it means the row cannot be scheduled as a window, so wireable is false.
problems.fix: Leave as is unless staff want a yearly replay; if so, create a reconstructed (R) season June 7 to Sept 3 and reuse no existing season name (Halloween is unrelated).

critiques.notes: Dates that matter are sourced: release June 7, 2010 (node/86237) and Pet Parade Sept 2-3, 2010, marked last Summer Camp event (article 1780). The start and end are not stated as the run's open and close dates, and the row already says so. Zones, NPCs and the two party quest titles are cited to article and locale ids I did not re-check here; the Jojo and place-name separations are reasonable caveats. The row is honest about its gaps and does not invent a cadence or clock time. Not wireable as a season or slot.

problems.issue: Season is null, so a builder has no window to load even though the single run has sources for both ends (release June 7, 2010; Pet Parade Sept 2-3, 2010, which I re-checked in article 1780 and it says it was the last Summer Camp event). The row defers the season decision entirely.
problems.fix: Draft a candidate season 'Summer Camp' 2010-06-07 to 2010-09-03 with the start marked (R) as the release date, not the first themed week, and the end marked as the last named event day. Keep it admin-gated until staff confirm.

problems.issue: 'one_off_replay' is not a kind value the calendar lens recognises. Staff-run seasonal events should be admin_only, not a free-standing one-off type.
problems.fix: Set recurrence to admin_only (one dated run, replayed only when staff start it), and name the season so it can be started by hand.

problems.issue: June 7 is confirmed as the release (tentonhammer node/86237), but the 13-week run and its 'week of the announcement' start are not dated in any source checked. Treating the release as the run start is an inference.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label on the start and cite the release date as the reason.

problems.issue: The existing Halloween season (Sept 20 - Nov 11) does not overlap June 7 - Sept 3, so there is no collision. No note on this was recorded.
problems.fix: Add a one-line check that the proposed window does not overlap Halloween.

critiques.notes: Calendar facts check out: the 2010 dates are internally consistent (start June 7, end Sept 3, same year, one run), and Pet Parade Sept 2-3 is confirmed in article 1780. The row is honest about the open items (no end-date statement, merge risk with the permanent place name at locale:442124, Pirate Week excluded). It is not wireable because it stops short of a season object. Summer Camp is a fixed-window, admin-started event, so it should become an admin_only season draft rather than remain null.

event.name: Free Realms Official First Birthday Yearbook

activities: watch the commemorative yearbook video recapping the features, games, pets and jobs introduced over the past year

revival.why: The evidence shows a published video, not a timed in-game event. No source dates the video, gives a season window, or gives a cadence, so it cannot be placed on a yearly season or a daily slot. Replay it as a media item, not as a scheduled event.

evidence.claim: Article 1320 announces a commemorative yearbook video that recaps the features, games, pets and jobs introduced over the past year. Its only date is the capture date, 2010-05-25, and it names no birthday.
The wiki has a file page for the First Birthday yearbook, in Category:Videos and Category:Games. The wiki page is the only source tying the title to the First Birthday.
evidence.source: wiki File:Free Realms Official First Birthday Yearbook (cited in event pack; the wiki gallery page for Bert/Ernie also cites the 2nd birthday video, not this one)

evidence.claim: The First Birthday celebration ran from April 29, 2010, with a party until May 10, 2010. This brackets the birthday, not the video's release date.
The 2nd Birthday yearbook is a separate video (wiki File:Free Realms 2nd Birthday Yearbook Video, Category:Videos). It is not part of this row.
evidence.source: lookup wiki: File:Free Realms 2nd Birthday Yearbook Video

open: No source dates the video's release, so original_dates is empty and no season window can be set. The yearbook could be placed in a 2010 spring window, but that would be (R) with no source.
Article 1320 is linked to the First Birthday only by the wiki title. The article itself does not name the birthday.
The 2nd Birthday yearbook video is a separate row and is not covered here. The pack's combined 'Free Realms yearbook video' name was split.
The pack's NPC appearances (Jolly Roger, Wraith, Chatty) are video cast from the wiki, not event content, so runs.npcs is empty.
No announcement text or locale id was found, so announce is null.

problems.issue: The row says article 1320 announces a yearbook video that recaps the past year. The articles.json record (article-1320, titled 'Free Realms - What is New?', captured 2010-05-25, date null) confirms that, but the record calls the video 'from the Free Realms team' and says nothing about a birthday. The article's own summary treats the capture date only as 'a dated marker that the game was about a year old'.
problems.fix: Keep the claim, but say the article is titled 'Free Realms - What is New?' and has date null. Say explicitly that the article is not linked to the First Birthday by any source except the wiki title.

problems.issue: I checked the wiki File page. Its indexed text shows only Category: Games and Category: Videos, with an empty description. It does not say the video is the First Birthday yearbook beyond the title itself. The row's wording suggests a stronger tie than the page supports.
problems.fix: Cite the File page for the title and categories only, and state that the page has no description text.

critiques.notes: Verified: article 2112 summary says a one-day Double Station Cash promotion on Saturday, April 30, framed as thanks for patience after a service interruption. Article 2119 summary (Spanish, late April 2011) matches the Saturday April 30 date across SOE games. TTH 97967 summary (April 2011, Saturday, Free Realms, EQ, EQ2) supports the 2011 year. April 30, 2011 was a Saturday. No Free Realms client or wiki tie to NPCs, zones or items, so empty runs are correct. Other Double Station Cash promos (Dec 2010, Back to School 2011, Europe Oct 2011, CVS 2012, 7-Eleven, Spring 2013) are correctly excluded. Recurrence of one_off_replay is sensible. The date claims are well sourced; the main weaknesses are the year being inferred and the narrowed reward wording.

problems.issue: The value 'one_off_replay' is a free-text label. I could not confirm it matches the scheduler's enumerated recurrence values, so a builder may need to map it.
problems.fix: Confirm the allowed recurrence enum and map this to the one-off value, keeping the 'do not repeat yearly' note.

problems.issue: The year 2011 rests on the April 2011 TTH coverage and the SOE notice captured 2011-06-04. The 2112 summary itself gives no year. The row says this, so it is a caveat, not an error.
problems.fix: Optional: read the 2112 article page to confirm the year directly.

critiques.notes: I checked the calendar. April 30, 2011 is a Saturday (Jan 1, 2011 was a Saturday; day 120 is 119 days later, a multiple of 7). The 2112 summary and the 2119 summary both say a one-day double Station Cash promotion on Saturday April 30, so the date is sourced in two places. The TTH 97967 entry (node 14824) says the Saturday event was held in April 2011. No other Double Station Cash promotion shares this date, and the other promotions in the pack (Dec 2010, Labor Day 2012, Spring 2013, Europe Oct 2011, CVS Jan 2012, Best Buy Aug 2013) are correctly excluded. A season window is not needed for a one-off, and no existing season name applies, so season null is right. The cause conflict (PSN breach versus April 21 intrusion) and the eligibility detail are not calendar issues and do not block the row.

original_dates.source: Start: articleIds 2118 and 2119 (lookup, Spanish: 'un día de doble Station Cash, el sábado 30 de abril'), confirmed this pass. End: articleId 2125 (pack-sourced only; lookup returned the 'from 4 AM to 3:59 AM Sunday May 1 Brasilia time' fact again, so the hours are the lookup's fact, not a re-read of the page). activities: Buy or use Station Cash during the one-day double window (eligible purchase types not confirmed)
rewards: Double Station Cash for the day (articleIds 2118, 2119)

announce.text: One-day double Station Cash on Saturday, April 30 across SOE's games, as a thank-you for player patience after a service interruption.

revival.why: A single dated promotion with no cadence or seasonal pattern. It is not a holiday, so it does not fit yearly_season. Replaying it needs a staff decision on each run, so admin_only is the fallback if the revival prefers staff control. No source gives a repeat schedule.

evidence.claim: SOE announced a one-day double Station Cash promotion on Saturday April 30 across its game lineup, as a thank-you for player patience

The promotion is cross-game (SOE's lineup, not Free Realms alone)

open: Eligible purchases (in-game Station Cash buys, card redemptions, or both) are unconfirmed. articleId 2112 is not verifiable, so no purchase rule is recorded.
The 4 AM to 3:59 AM Brasilia hours come from articleId 2125 via the pack and lookup, not from a direct re-read of the Portuguese page. Confirm before using the hours.

Separate promotions are excluded: 2893 (Spring Celebration, March 29-31 2011, which holds the SMS-exclusion rule), 2763, 1970, 2294, 1590, 346, 1186, TTH 74525, and the CVS, Walgreens and Best Buy offers.

problems.issue: The row says the service-interruption and apology framing is not in 2118/2119. Lookup's summaries of those posts do mention it: 2118 'apologizes for the outage' and 2119 'apologizing for a recent service interruption'. The claim is under-sourced, not false.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: 2011-04-30 is a Saturday and 2011-05-01 is the Sunday, so the start and end dates agree with the day names in the sources. The hours are consistent with the time zones: 4 AM Brasilia (UTC-3) is 8 AM Portugal in late April/May (WEST, UTC+1). A one-off dated promotion with no season is correct, and season null is right because Halloween does not match. one_off_replay with admin_only as the fallback is a sensible recurrence. The row is wireable as a single dated window (2011-04-30 to 2011-05-01, date-only if the hours stay unconfirmed). The separate promotions are correctly excluded and no season name is reused.

activities: Buy Station Cash housing items and building lots at 50% off during the Presidents' Day weekend sale window

A sale is a time-limited store promotion, so it can be replayed once on its original window by staff rather than scheduled as a yearly season. A 2012 run is only suggested by the unverified client banner locale:614 and is not added.

evidence.claim: Presidents' Day weekend sale: all Station Cash housing items and building lots 50% off, noon Feb 18 to 23:59 PST Feb 21, 2011
Same sale, same window, stated again (Spanish text, exact window given)
Small house (Thorn/Thorny Forest) and Solitary Island lot listed among featured housing items
Pre-launch notices (2037, 2038) describe an SOE multi-game Presidents' Day promotion with possible Bonus XP and discounts; they do not confirm Free Realms Bonus XP, so no XP reward is listed
Client string 'President's Day Sale!' exists but is flagged not_live and has no article tie

open: No recurrence evidence: a 2012 or later run is unverified. locale:614 (flagged not_live, expired Feb 2012) is a client banner with no article link; it needs an article check before any further occurrence is added.
Small house name variant: 2039 says Thorn Forest, 2040 says Thorny Forest. Confirm the in-game zone name.
Sale base prices are not in any source, so item prices are null. The discount rule covers all Station Cash housing items and lots, not only the two named items.
Article 2037 has no absolute date; the 2011 year comes from 2039 and 2040 only.
Solitary Island lot: the client item 'Lonely Island Lot' (article 1818) is a different update and is not merged. The article 2131 lifetime-member plot offer is a separate promotion and is not merged.
No zones, NPCs, quests or wiki/video evidence were found for this event.

problems.issue: The evidence list cites locale:614 (and 1417) as a source. The automatic id check flags locale:614 as not_live (expired promotional banner). It has no article tie, so it is not evidence for the event.

problems.fix: Rewrite as: only one dated run (2011) is evidenced by articles 2039 and 2040; no article says it recurs; a 2012 run is unverified and not added.

critiques.notes: I checked the core facts with the articles lookup. Articles 2039 (English summary) and 2040 (Spanish text) both state a Presidents' Day weekend sale with all Station Cash housing items and building lots at 50% off, ending 23:59 PST February 21, 2011, and both name the small house and the Solitary Island lot. The window is dated and sourced, so a builder can load it as a one-off replay. The row's main risk is citation hygiene: it leans on flagged locale:614 in three places, which should be removed. Item prices, zones, and NPCs are correctly left null or empty and marked open. The 2037 pre-launch notice is correctly kept out of the reward list.

problems.issue: Cites locale:614, which the automatic id check flags as not_live (expired promotional banner). The sentence only notes it as a non-added 2012 hint, but it should not sit in the rationale as a source.
problems.fix: Drop the locale:614 reference from revival.why and state only that no article evidences a 2012 or later run.

problems.issue: Repeats the flagged locale:614 as the basis for checking a 2012 run.

problems.issue: Both are null. The original_dates are sourced (articles 2039 and 2040 agree on Feb 18 noon to Feb 21 23:59 PST 2011), but there is no season window or slot cadence, so a builder has no shape to load.

event.name: Double Station Cash Day (service interruption apology)

original_dates.source: Start day: Saturday April 30 per tentonhammer.com/node/97967 (Double Station Cash event on Saturday for Free Realms after a PSN security-breach service interruption). Window 4 AM Sat Apr 30 to 3:59 AM Sun May 1 Brasilia time is from freerealms.com article 2125 as reported in the pack; NOT re-verified, article 2125 did not return in my index lookup (R: end date taken from the pack's 2125 window, unverified). Year 2011: the pack cites tentonhammer node/97837 and 97892 for April 2011 and April 21 interruption; not re-checked here.

rewards: Double Station Cash (Station Cash bonus day). The mechanic (purchases, card redemptions, or both) is not confirmed by any source I could check; do not assume.

revival.why: A single dated Station Cash promotion tied to one April 2011 service-interruption make-good. No source says it recurs, and it is not a holiday or season, so it does not go on the yearly season calendar or a daily slot.

evidence.claim: Tentonhammer reports SOE offered a Double Station Cash event on a Saturday for Free Realms players as compensation for a service interruption after a PlayStation Network security breach.
Article 2893 is a Spring Celebration Double Station Cash weekend, March 29-31, 2013, not 2011. It is excluded from this row.
evidence.source: http://www.freerealms.com:80/article/detail.action?articleId=2893 (verified in lookup: 'from March 29 to March 31, 2013', 12:01 AM PDT Mar 29 to 11:59 PM PDT Mar 31, 2013)

evidence.claim: The late-December Double Station Cash weekend (article 1970) ran until December 19, 11:59pm PST, purchases doubled. Excluded from this row.
A 2011 Europe pre-paid card redemption double promo ran Oct 7-10, 2011. Excluded from this row.
The PS3 'repair' make-good plan in articles 2118/2119 is a separate plan, not a live event, and is excluded.
evidence.source: pack note on freerealms.com articles 2118/2119; not re-verified in index

open: Articles 2112, 2118, 2119 and 2125 did not return in my index lookup, so their text, dates and the April 30 - May 1 Brasilia window are unverified. The row rests on the Tentonhammer 97967 Saturday report plus the pack's readings of those articles. Confirm them before wiring.
Article 2118's index capture date (2011-06-04) is a capture date, not a post date, so it does not contradict the April year. Confirm before relying on it.
Spring Celebration is 2013 (article 2893), not 2011 as the previous answer said. The previous answer's evidence line is wrong and should be corrected. Keep it out of this row.
No announcement text is recorded. The announce field is null until 2112 or 2119 is read and dated.
No season is defined; the Halloween row is unrelated. Wire as a dated one-time promotion, not a yearly season or daily slot.
Mechanic and scope are unresolved. Portfolio-wide scope is from the pack (2125), not verified here. Items, NPCs, quests, zones and activities stay empty; no source I checked ties them to this event.

problems.issue: The source string cites articles 2118 and 2119 as proof the event ran on April 30. Both are future-tense announcements ('will be hosting', 'announced'). Only 2125 and the Ten Ton Hammer report say it ran, and 2125's article date is still unknown.
problems.fix: Cite 2118 and 2119 only for the announcement and 2125 plus node/97967 for the run. Keep the run date as the Saturday 2011-04-30 claim.

problems.issue: The announce field is null, but 2118 and 2119 announce the day. The announcement date is unresolved because 2118's index date conflicts with an April announcement (2011-06-04 in the summary).
problems.fix: Fill announce with the 2118/2119 announcement as a source-backed fact and mark its date as unverified, or record the conflicting index date explicitly.

problems.issue: The row has no season or slot and only a single original_dates entry whose year rests on the Saturday wording and TTH's 'April 2011' rather than a dated article. A builder has no window it can load with confidence until the article dates are confirmed.
problems.fix: Confirm the 2125 article date and the 2118 date conflict, then mark the row wireable as a one-time dated window (kind promotion, one_off_replay).

problems.issue: The source says 'April 2011' and 'Saturday' but gives no day number. The April 30 date comes from SOE's own posts, so the TTH claim supports the year and the event, not the exact day.
problems.fix: Attribute the exact day to 2118/2119/2125 and the year and event to node/97967, with the 'Saturday' wording noted as corroboration.

critiques.notes: I confirmed in the index that 2118, 2119 and 2125 all name a one-day Double Station Cash promotion on Saturday April 30 across SOE's games, and that TTH 97967 ties it to Free Realms after a PSN-breach interruption. April 30, 2011 was a Saturday, which supports the year. The row is factually sound as far as it goes, and the open list is honest about the missing mechanic, article dates and empty fields. Its weak points are the announcement-versus-run citations and the unresolved 2118 date conflict, which block a clean wire.

problems.issue: Recorded as 2011-04-30, but article 2125 (checked via lookup) gives the run as 4 AM Sat April 30 to 3:59 AM Sun May 1, Brasilia time. The row's own source text admits the window crosses into May 1, yet the end date is forced to the same day. That is a calendar mismatch: in UTC the run ends 2011-05-01 06:59.
problems.fix: Set end to 2011-05-01 and carry the window as start 2011-04-30 04:00 and end 2011-05-01 03:59 America/Sao_Paulo (or as UTC 07:00 Apr 30 to 06:59 May 1). Drop the note that forces a same-day end.

problems.issue: The answer says the Spring Celebration Double Station Cash ran March 29-31, 2011. The schedule pack (quest-lines/schedule-packs.json, article 2893 summary) dates the Spring Celebration weekend to March 29-31, 2013. The year conflicts, and the answer gives no source for 2011. This is an excluded event, but the claim is wrong as stated and could mislead a later merge.
problems.fix: Correct the year to 2013 for the Spring Celebration, or cite the source that gives 2011. Keep it out of this row either way.

problems.issue: The article 2118 summary gives a capture date of 2011-06-04 and 2119 is 'roughly late April 2011'. The April year is backed by tentonhammer node 97967 (Saturday, April 2011) and the April 21 interruption, which is enough for 2011. The 2118 capture date is a capture, not a post date, so it does not contradict the year, but the open note should say so.
problems.fix: Note that 2011-06-04 is the capture date for 2118, not the post date, and that the year rests on the Tentonhammer April 2011 post.

problems.issue: one_off_replay is correct. The date is a Saturday (2011-04-30 is a Saturday, verified), and no source says it recurs. It does not belong on the season calendar.
problems.fix: No change.

problems.issue: season null is correct. No season is defined and none should be reused; Halloween is unrelated.
problems.fix: No change.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: 2011-04-30 is a Saturday, and the Saturday wording in articles 2118, 2119, 2125 and the Tentonhammer report agree on April 30 across sources. The main defect is the end date, which is set to the start day when the cited window runs to 3:59 AM May 1 Brasilia. Fix that and the row is a sound one-off dated window, so it is wireable as a single dated occurrence with explicit times. The Spring Celebration year error sits in the evidence, not in the row's dates, but it should be corrected.

problems.issue: The row says article 2112 did not return in the index. It does: articles/articles.json:14843-14854 (captured 2011-07-15, date field 2011-04-30, title 'Saturday Only! Double Station Cash'). Its summary says the promotion was a one-day Double Station Cash on Saturday April 30 as a thank-you for patience during the interruption, and that game cards can be redeemed for Station Cash or Station Cash bought via the SOE account. That is the closest source on mechanic and scope.
problems.fix: Cite article 2112 as an announcement source with its date field, and note its channels (card redemption and account purchase) as a source-stated scope, while leaving the exact doubling rule open since the summary gives only 'double'.

problems.issue: The 2011 year rests on the Ten Ton Hammer 97967 report, which carries an explicit date field of 2011-04-29 (articles.json:14821). The row instead leans on the 97837/97892 interruption pages, which are weaker for the day. The 2112 year is explicitly 'inferred', not stated.
problems.fix: Cite node/97967 with its 2011-04-29 date as the year anchor and say 2112's year is inferred.

problems.issue: The 4 AM Sat to 3:59 AM Sun May 1 Brasilia window is in articles/facts.json:15222 (statement, attributed to article 2125, whose date is null). It is sourced, not invented, but the row marks it only as 'unverified'. The window times are also absent from the row's fields.
problems.fix: Keep the end date 2011-05-01 with the facts.json:15222 citation, and record the window as 04:00 to 03:59 Brasilia time (07:00 to 06:59 UTC) rather than leaving it in prose. Drop the 'NOT re-verified' wording since the fact record exists.

problems.issue: Empty fields are correct: no source ties NPCs, quests or items to the event. The 'do not assume' mechanic note is adequate but should cite 2112's card and account channels.
problems.fix: No change beyond the mechanic citation above.

critiques.notes: The core row is sourced: a one-day Double Station Cash on Saturday April 30, 2011 (Ten Ton Hammer 2011-04-29; articles 2112/2119/2125), portfolio-wide, with the PS3 repair plan correctly excluded. The Spring 2013, December 1970 and Oct 2011 Europe promos are correctly excluded. The one-time recurrence is sensible and no season is needed. Wireable as a dated one-off promotion with the window times above.

problems.issue: The row says article 2125 did not return and that its April 30 to May 1 Brasilia window is unverified (marked R). The index now returns article 2125's summary and the 'articles' fact: a Station Cash double day on Saturday April 30, 4 AM to 3:59 AM Sunday May 1 Brasilia time (8 AM to 7:59 AM Portugal). The window is sourced, so the (R) marker and the 'do not wire until confirmed' caveat are stale.
problems.fix: Cite articles/2125 as the source of the window, drop the (R) tag on the end date, and keep only the caveat that the mechanic is unresolved.

problems.issue: The value 'one_off_replay' is not an obvious scheduler enum and the reason is fine but the field does not say how a builder should load a single window. Calendar-wise the one-off choice is correct: one dated occurrence, no season, no slot.
problems.fix: Use a one-off dated window value the scheduler already accepts (for example one_off with the single start and end), or note the enum it maps to.

problems.issue: The year 2011 rests on Ten Ton Hammer node 97892/97837 and the 2011 Tentonhammer 'Double Station Cash on Saturday... April 2011' report (line about SOE after PSN breach). The pack's dates line up: April 30, 2011 is a Saturday, and the Brasilia/Portugal offset (UTC-3 vs UTC+1) matches 4 AM to 8 AM. Confirmed.
problems.fix: None needed beyond citing the Tentonhammer summary alongside 97967.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: April 30, 2011 is a Saturday, so original_dates is correct. The Spring Celebration correction is right: article 2893 is March 29-31, 2013, and the pack's 2011 label is wrong. The December weekend (article 1970, valid to December 19) and the October 7-10, 2011 Europe card window are correctly excluded, and no other 2011 dates collide with the April window. Season null is correct: no season or yearly slot exists for a one-off promotion. Scope is portfolio-wide (multiple SOE games), which the row keeps as a note without inventing Free Realms-only items. The mechanic (purchases vs card redemptions) remains open; the 'Saturday Only! Double Station Cash' summary hints at card redemption too, so it is correctly left unresolved. The row is wireable as a dated one-time promotion.
