problems.issue: The field holds 2010-10-21, which the source (articleId=1864) gives only as one Sanctuary Trick or Treat party session. The answer's own source note says run start is not in evidence. Presenting it as the run start is a calendar error. Other 2010 dated sessions exist: Fri Oct 1 9am PT (articleId 1830), Thu Oct 7 3pm PT Ghostly Pet Party (1845), Fri Oct 8 (1849), Thu Oct 14 3pm PT and Fri Oct 15 9am PT (1851), Thu Oct 21 3pm PT (1864). The answer's claim of 'no clock times' for 2010 is contradicted by these.
problems.fix: Set 2010 start and end to null, or to 2010-10-01 as the earliest dated session with a note that it is a session, not a run window. List the session dates in a separate sessions field. Do not treat Oct 21 as the run start.

problems.issue: The answer creates no slot or weekly row and says the 2010 community events have no clock times. Sources give fixed times: Friday 9:00am Pacific on Server 1 (Oct 1, 15) and Thursday 3:00pm Pacific on Server 1 (Oct 7, 14, 21). That is a weekly cadence with clock times, and it was left out.
problems.fix: Record 2010 as a dated community session list (Thu 15:00 PT and Fri 09:00 PT, Server 1, Oct 2010) with source ids 1830, 1845, 1849, 1851, 1864, or mark it open with a reason. Do not leave it as 'no cadence'.

problems.issue: The window Oct 1 to Nov 23 is widened to fit the 2011 end date, and it reuses the existing 'Halloween' season name. That name also covers the client Halloween area set (Halloween_Pixiewood_1-10, Briarwood, Snowhill, StillWater) and the existing row Sep 20 to Nov 11 (R). Changing the shared row changes other Halloween content, which the answer does not address. The window is wide and rests on one end date (2011 Nov 23). The 2013 run (Oct 1 to Nov 12) is confirmed by articleId 2949 and the wiki, and the 2009 run by a pre-event article only.
problems.fix: Either create a separate season key (e.g. 'Super Spooktacular') with Oct 1 to Nov 23 and a note that it is an event window, or keep 'Halloween' and get staff sign-off that changing it does not affect the client area sets. Mark the 2009 window as pre-event and the 2011 end as the only source for Nov 23.

problems.issue: The automatic id check flags locale:2528 as a fragment with no quest meaning. Using it as evidence for the event name is not live evidence.
problems.fix: Drop that evidence item, or cite articleIds 1861, 2949 and the wiki title as the name sources.

problems.issue: 'yearly_season' is sensible for the Halloween holiday, but the 2010 timed sessions are repeating activities on weekday slots, and the answer does not record them as such. The kind is right, but the row is incomplete on the slot side.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season for the season window and add the 2010 Thu/Fri community sessions as a separate slot row with sources, or mark them open.

critiques.notes: Dates for 2011 (Oct 13 to Nov 23) and 2013 (Oct 1 to Nov 12) match the pack. The 2009 window is a pre-event schedule, and 2012 has no dates, so both stay unconfirmed. The season row is wireable as a window only after the conflict with the existing Halloween row is settled. The 2010 handling is the main defect: a party day is used as a run start, and the timed sessions are dropped.

problems.issue: The proposed window Oct 1 to Nov 23 is a union of 2009, 2011 and 2013 runs, marked (R). It is sourced, but Nov 23 comes only from 2011 and Oct 1 only from 2013, so the window is wider than any single run. The shared Halloween client-area set and the existing Sep 20 to Nov 11 (R) row also conflict with it.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label with the union rationale. Before applying, get staff sign-off on changing the shared Halloween row, or add a separate season key 'super-spooktacular' with the Oct 1 to Nov 23 window so the client Halloween area set is not touched.

problems.issue: Dated only from a pre-event schedule (tentonhammer node/75739). A second source, articleId 476, says the Halloween event 'ran' Oct 14 to Nov 11, but it is also worded as scheduled, so the run itself is still unconfirmed.
problems.fix: Keep the source note that the run is unconfirmed. The articleId 476 source can be cited as corroboration of the schedule, not of the actual run.

problems.issue: yearly_season is reasonable for an annual October-into-November event with shifting dates. No slot or weekly cadence is invented, which is correct.
problems.fix: None needed.

problems.issue: The automatic id check flags locale:2528 as a fragment. The answer already drops it from evidence and relies on articleIds 1861, 2949 and the wiki title, which I confirmed (2949 names 'Fourth Annual Super Spooktacular').
problems.fix: Cite articleId 2949 or 1861 for the name instead of locale:2528.

critiques.notes: I spot-checked the articles index. 2011 (articleId 2304): Oct 13 to Nov 23, 2011, confirmed, including the Vampires vs Werewolves Dance-Off. 2013 (articleId 2949): Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2013, confirmed. 2009: scheduled Oct 14 to Nov 11 (tentonhammer 75739, also articleId 476 wording), confirmed as scheduled, run unconfirmed. 2010 and 2012 have no dated window and are correctly left null. The 2010 party dates (Oct 21 and 22) were not re-verified in this pass; they rest on the pack's index check. The row is honest about its gaps and makes no invented clock times. The main risk is the calendar conflict with the existing Halloween season, which the row already flags.

problems.issue: The proposed Halloween window (Oct 1 to Nov 23) replaces the existing Halloween season row (Sep 20 to Nov 11) rather than adding to it. Changing that row also changes the shared Halloween client area set (Halloween_Pixiewood_1-10, Briarwood, Snowhill, StillWater), which other Halloween content may depend on. The answer flags this but still proposes the change as the window.
problems.fix: Do not overwrite the existing row. Either get staff sign-off and record the widened window explicitly, or keep the existing 'Halloween' season and add a separate season key 'super-spooktacular' with the proposed Oct 1 to Nov 23 window, so the client area set is untouched.

problems.issue: The window is justified as covering 2009, 2011 and 2013. Only the 2013 range (articleId=2949, Oct 1 to Nov 12) re-checked cleanly in the articles index. I could not reproduce the 2011 Oct 13 to Nov 23 range from articleId=2304 in lookup, and 2009 is a pre-event schedule that was never confirmed as run. The (R) tag is present, but the 2011 end date (Nov 23) is what drives the window's end, so it needs its own check.
problems.fix: Verify articleId=2304 directly for the 2011 start and end. If it cannot be confirmed, state the window as covering 2013 and 2009 only, or mark Nov 23 as (R) with that reason.

problems.issue: Both have null start and end. The 2010 party sessions are dated but are not a window, and the 2012 entry is only wiki-based. Both are honestly marked as open, which is acceptable.
problems.fix: No change needed; keep them open.

problems.issue: The name is said to be supported by articleIds 1861 and 2949 and the wiki title. The automatic check flags locale:2528 as a fragment, and the answer drops it, which is correct. The name is still well supported by the articles, so the name itself is fine.
problems.fix: Keep locale:2528 out of the evidence. Cite only the articles and wiki for the name.

problems.issue: yearly_season is the right kind for an annual October into November event with shifting dates. No slot or weekly row is needed.
problems.fix: No change.

critiques.notes: The calendar reasoning is sound: a yearly season, no invented clock times, 2010 and 2012 left open, and the name reuses the existing 'Halloween' season. The blocker is the unresolved overwrite of the existing Sep 20 to Nov 11 row, which touches shared client areas, so a builder cannot load it safely yet. Once staff choose between widening the existing row and adding a separate key, and the 2011 end date is confirmed, the row would be wireable.

problems.issue: Proposed Halloween window (Oct 1 to Nov 23) overwrites the existing 'Halloween' season row (Sep 20 to Nov 11). That row feeds the shared Halloween client area set (Halloween_Pixiewood_1-10, Briarwood, Snowhill, StillWater), so the change would affect non-event Halloween content. The answer itself says staff must confirm, so the row cannot be loaded as a clean season window yet.
problems.fix: Either get staff sign-off to replace the Halloween window with Oct 1 to Nov 23, or keep the existing Halloween row and add a separate season key 'super-spooktacular' with the proposed window. Record the decision in the row before wiring.

problems.issue: Marked 'run unconfirmed' and sourced only to a tentonhammer pre-event schedule. Articles index has an official SOE post, articleId=476 ('First Annual Super Spooktacular... running October 14 through November 11', free to registered players). The 2009 window is therefore sourced, not reconstructed.
problems.fix: Cite articleId=476 for 2009 Oct 14 to Nov 11 and drop the 'unconfirmed' wording. Keep tentonhammer as secondary.

problems.issue: Articles say 2013 was the 'Fourth Annual' (articleId=2949) and 2010 was the 'second' (articleId=1861). Counting 2009 as first, 2013 would be fifth. Either 2012 or 2010 is not counted the same way. The row mixes edition numbers and years without saying which.
problems.fix: Keep edition numbers out of the calendar. Add a note that the edition count is inconsistent across sources, and key the event by year only.

problems.issue: The name is said to be dropped from locale:2528 because it is a flagged fragment, yet the row still cites that locale match in its reasoning. The automatic id check flags it as not live evidence. The name itself is supported by articleIds, so the citation should not be used as evidence.
problems.fix: Remove the locale:2528 reference from the name justification and cite articleIds 1861, 2949 and 476 instead.

problems.issue: The '(R)' reason is present, but the statement that the window 'covers every dated full run' relies on 2009 being unconfirmed. Now that 476 confirms 2009, the claim holds, though the 2010 and 2012 windows are still undated.
problems.fix: Restate the window reason with the 2009 article, 2011 and 2013 dates. Note that 2010 and 2012 are assumed to fall in October and are not in evidence.

problems.issue: yearly_season is sensible for an annual October event. The 2010 party sessions are correctly not turned into a weekly or slot row.
problems.fix: No change needed.

critiques.notes: Calendar lens. Year-by-year dates for 2009, 2011 and 2013 are sourced and agree with the proposed window: each run falls inside Oct 1 to Nov 23 and the window does not swallow unrelated months. The blocker is the shared Halloween season conflict, which needs staff decision, not evidence. 2010 and 2012 are correctly left with null start and end. Score 5 because the row is honest about its gaps but cannot be wired until the season conflict is resolved and the 2009 source is updated.

season.name: Festival of Hearts
season.source: (R) Month range only: wiki:Festival of Hearts says the event is 'held from February through March in Merry Vale'. No source gives a day-level start or end. Feb 1 and Mar 31 are month boundaries chosen to match that wording. This window was not fitted to the 2014 Game Update 128 listing (02/04/2014), which is a listing date only. Name is new; the only defined season, Halloween, is a different event.

original_dates.source: Start: freerealms.com article 967 update notes, dated 2010-02-12 in refs articles/articles.json:11674, announce the Festival of Hearts in Merry Vale. Article 965 (refs articles.json:11716) says the festival would come online after testing. Length: the SOE press release dated 2010-02-08 (articles.json:11604) previews a 'month-long' Festival of Hearts. End day not sourced. The 2010-02-12 semi-formal dance (article 960, articles.json:11697-11702) is a separate community event, and article 957 is unverified.

Not a dated occurrence. Article 2501 is a PS3-era return post with only a relative timestamp ('6 months, 1 week ago' at the 2012-08-19 capture), giving an approximate early-2012 inference. The wiki Events note that a presents event started in 2012 conflicts with the 2010/2011 mentions and is unresolved.

wiki:Template:News lists Festival of Hearts in the Game Update 128 overview dated 02/04/2014. This is a listing date only; no article or wiki text confirms the festival start day. wiki:Festival of Hearts gives February through March.

revival.why: Only one year (2010) has an article-dated start. Articles 969 and 2016 call the event 'annual', and 2500, 2501 and 2016 say it 'returned', but these are undated posts and support a yearly pattern without confirming it. The 2012 year is inferred and conflicts with the wiki Events note. The 2014 start is a wiki listing date. Until a second article-dated year is found, run it as an admin-started season. yearly_season is the candidate recurrence once confirmed.

The annual Festival of Hearts has begun in Merry Vale (undated post). 'Annual' is wording only.
The annual Festival of Hearts has returned to Merry Vale (undated post).
The festival returned to Merry Vale with daily and members-only quests (undated post). Article 2500 uses 'seasonal celebration'.
The festival launched for PS3 on the day of the post (undated).
A community semi-formal Festival of Hearts dance was held Friday 12 February 2010. It is a community event, not the festival window.
Developer blog February 2010 featured the Festival of Hearts (teaser only; full text not checked).

The festival runs February through March in Merry Vale.

open: Calendar evidence is month-level only (February, plus 2010 with a start day). No year has a sourced end day, and 2012 and 2014 have no confirmed start day.

Recurrence is not confirmed. Only 2010 is article-dated; 'annual' and 'returned' wording in undated posts (969, 2016, 2500, 2501) is supporting, not dated evidence. Keep admin_only until a second article-dated year is found.
2012 is inferred from a relative timestamp only (article 2501). The wiki Events note saying a presents event started in 2012 conflicts with the 2010/2011 mentions and is unresolved.
2011 is a single wiki mention (Gifting Basket: Cupid, Heart Critter); not dated by an article and not counted toward recurrence.
Article 957 is unverified for the 2010 dance; 960 is the cited source.
Item prices are not in any source. All are null; currency labels come from wiki wording ('SC Marketplace'). Item lists are undated, so do not treat them as one live set.

Regional variants (articles 2018, 2019, 2026, 1057 for Vegalegre, Joyful Valley, Rois/Araiana, Valentin) are not merged. Cudip is placed in Joyful Valley (articles 1053 and the French post), not Merry Vale, so he is not listed as a Merry Vale NPC.
Excluded: Dubawug (locale:70967), Softening the Stone (locale:427157), Beloved Bow (unverified), Lovasus and Emo-Tor (not in category), locale:3545 and 3559 (placeholders).
No slot or weekly cadence is sourced, so slots and weekly are null. No announce text is sourced.
Live status is unsure, and the rebuild's target year is not set.
answer._critique_fixes: Removed the claim that the 2014 festival began 2014-02-04 (it is a listing date). Removed the claim that the season window was built to cover 2014. Cited 960 for the dance and marked 957 unverified. Stated that the calendar has month-level evidence only. Reworded the recurrence reasoning and added the 2012 conflict to 'why'.

problems.issue: Contradicts the row's own open[0] and season.source, which say the 02/04/2014 date is a Game Update 128 listing date and is not confirmed as the festival start. original_dates[2014] leaves start null. The evidence line states a start the calendar does not record.
problems.fix: Reword the evidence line to 'Game Update 128 overview listed Festival of Hearts on 02/04/2014 (wiki); start day not confirmed', matching open[0].

problems.issue: Feb 1 is chosen so the window 'covers' the 2014-02-04 Game Update listing. That fits the window to a non-start date. The only sourced fact is the wiki's 'February through March' wording, so the day-level start is not supported by any dated festival start.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label but state the basis as the wiki month range only (February through March). Drop the claim that the window was built to cover 2014-02-04, or state it as a choice, not a source.

problems.issue: Cites articleId=957 for the 2010-02-12 dance, while the index and the pack's own note show the dance as articleId=960. The 957 citation is unverified, and the calendar row cites both as if they agree.
problems.fix: Cite only articleId=960 for the dance and mark 957 as unverified or remove it. Keep 1003 as the teaser 'February 2010' source, flagged as unverified.

problems.issue: No year has a start or end day. 2010 is a teaser summary, 2012 is an inferred relative time, and 2014 is a wiki listing. The entries cannot confirm the season window or show yearly agreement, so they add little calendar evidence beyond the month range.
problems.fix: State plainly that the calendar has month-level evidence only (Feb, 2010/2012/2014) and no day-level dated occurrence. Do not present the 2012 entry as a date; list it under open.

problems.issue: The row says yearly recurrence is 'not yet confirmed', yet articles 969 and 2016 use the word 'annual' and 2016/2500/2501 say 'returned'. That text supports a yearly pattern. The row also omits the conflicting wiki Events note (presents event in 2012) when it discusses the 2012 year.
problems.fix: Cite the 'annual'/'returned' wording as supporting but not dated evidence, keep admin_only, and mention the unresolved 2012 conflict in the why field.

problems.issue: The automatic id check flags locale:3545 as a placeholder. The row lists it only as excluded, so it is not used as evidence. Still, it should not appear as a festival-linked id at all.
problems.fix: Keep it out of the item and evidence lists; the excluded note is fine as is.

critiques.notes: Calendar lens. The row is honest about gaps: it marks the Feb 1 to Mar 31 window as (R), keeps recurrence admin_only, and does not wire a yearly schedule. Season name is new and does not reuse Halloween, which is right. The wiki month range 'February through March' is a sourced basis for a manual admin-started season, so wireable is true for that use only, not as yearly_season. The main defects are the 2014 start contradiction in evidence, the 957/960 citation mismatch, and the window being tuned to a listing date rather than a festival start. Fix those and the row can pass.

problems.issue: 2010-02-12 is the date of update notes (article 967) that announce the event. It is not sourced as the festival's start. The row labels an announcement date as the start, and the answer's own text admits the 2010 end is unsourced. The 2010 start is therefore not established.
problems.fix: Record 2010-02-12 as announcement_date (update notes, article 967). Set the 2010 start to null or 'February 2010 (unspecified day)' until a source gives the start day.

problems.issue: 2014-02-04 is the Game Update 128 listing date. The answer's own text says it is 'not a confirmed festival start', yet it fills the start field. The pack's evidence line also says 'began February 4, 2014', which contradicts the answer.
problems.fix: Move 2014-02-04 to a listing_date field, set start to null, and correct the evidence line so it does not say the festival began that day.

problems.issue: Feb 1 to Mar 31 is a (R) reconstruction from a wiki month range, and the 2010 evidence is 'month-long' with no day. The (R) mark and reason are present, which is acceptable, but no dated source supports either day. The 2010 and 2014 instances do not confirm the window, since their starts are not established.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) window but state that no dated start or end exists, so the window is a month-range guess. Do not present it as a source-backed season window.

problems.issue: admin_only is sensible given that only one article-dated occurrence (announcement, 2010) exists. The yearly pattern rests on undated 'annual' wording in articles 969 and 2016.
problems.fix: No change to the value. Note that 'annual' wording is undated and cannot count as a second occurrence.

problems.issue: The dance is cited as article 957 in the answer. The pack says 957 is unverified and the index shows 960. Its claim also says 'first annual' dance, which the answer treats as a separate community event but still lists in original_dates sources.
problems.fix: Cite article 960 only, and keep it out of the festival window sources.

problems.issue: Locale:3545 is flagged as a placeholder. The answer already excludes it in open, so this is not a fault, but the open list still lists the Cudip and presents-in-2012 conflicts without a resolution plan.
problems.fix: Keep the exclusions. Add the 2012 presents conflict to the reason the row is not wireable.

critiques.notes: Row is not wireable. The only solid dated fact is that update notes dated 2010-02-12 (article 967) announced the festival, and 2014-02-04 is a wiki listing date. Neither is a verified start, and no end date exists in any source. The admin_only recurrence is correct. Fix the start fields before any yearly or season schedule is loaded; a 'start unknown, February announced' record would be the honest state.

problems.issue: The Feb 1 to Mar 31 window is an (R) reconstruction from the wiki's 'February through March' wording. The only dated run, 2010, is sourced as a 'month-long' event starting in the week of Feb 8 (TTH node/80708, SOE press release articles.json:11604) and starting Feb 12 (article 967). That implies roughly one month, so Mar 31 may overstate the run by about two weeks. The answer does not mention this conflict.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label but add the 'month-long' 2010 evidence and the Feb 8 kickoff week to the reason. State that Mar 31 is an upper bound, and that the window is for admin-started seasons only.

problems.issue: Article 957 is in the index and is a sourced dance announcement (articles.json:11697 and 17834 Spanish, 957 summary: 'first annual' dance, Friday Feb 12 2010). The answer calls it unverified. The 960 citation is correct but the 957 caveat is overstated.
problems.fix: Cite 957 and 960 together for the dance and drop the 'unverified' caveat on 957.

problems.issue: The 2010-02-12 start is supported by article 967's summary ('live in Merry Vale starting with the February 12, 2010 update'). The answer's wording, 'announce... festival', is fine, but the 2010 kickoff is also reported as the week of Feb 8 by TTH. The conflict is not noted.
problems.fix: Note that the 2010 start is Feb 12 per the update notes, with a Feb 8 week kickoff per TTH and the press release.

problems.issue: admin_only is sensible: only 2010 is article-dated, and the 'annual' and 'returned' wording is undated. The 2012 and 2014 starts are inferred or listing-only.
problems.fix: No change. Keep yearly_season as the candidate once a second dated year is found.

problems.issue: The automatic id check flags locale:3545 as a placeholder. The answer only lists it as excluded, so it is not used as evidence. No change to the row is needed.
problems.fix: None required; keep the exclusion note.

critiques.notes: The 2010 February start, the Merry Vale zone, the 'annual' wording and the admin_only recurrence all check out against the articles index. The main calendar weakness is that the season end is month-level only and Mar 31 may overrun a roughly month-long 2010 run; this is labeled (R), so the row is true as far as it goes. The season window is wireable as an admin-started season with the (R) label. Slots and weekly are correctly null.

problems.issue: The row treats 2012 as inferred only from article 2501's relative timestamp and says the wiki Events note conflicts. It misses a dated wiki source: Template:News/Archive has an 'Update of February 7, 2012' entry whose text says 'Merry Vale is celebrating the Festival of Hearts'. That is a dated, if thin, 2012 occurrence and should be cited or explicitly rejected.
problems.fix: Add the wiki Template:News/Archive 'Update of February 7, 2012' Festival of Hearts entry as a 2012 source (start 2012-02-07, wiki-only, end null). Keep the inferred article 2501 note as secondary, and say why the Events-page conflict is still open.

problems.issue: The 2010 press release calls the event 'month-long', while the season window and wiki say February through March. The row states the end is unsourced but does not note this tension with the Feb-Mar window.
problems.fix: Note that 'month-long' (2010-02-08 release) points to roughly Feb 12 to mid-March 2010, and that this does not confirm Mar 31. Keep the window marked (R).

problems.issue: The article 967 'starting with the February 12, 2010 update' wording (articles.json:11674 summary) supports the 2010 start directly; the row cites it only as update notes. Acceptable, but the sourced line should quote the start phrase.
problems.fix: Quote article 967's 'live ... starting with the February 12, 2010 update' wording in the evidence entry.

critiques.notes: Most claims check out: article 967 and the 2010-02-08 release are real in the pack; article 960 is the 12 Feb 2010 community dance, with 957 unverified. 'Annual' and 'returned' come from undated posts 969, 2016 and 2500 and are correctly marked as supporting only. The Feb-Mar window is correctly marked (R) with a reason, and it does not swallow Halloween's season. The 2014 start is correctly kept as a listing date. problems.issue: The Dec 9 start is a reconstruction. The only support is that the Dec 9, 2010 party was called 'the first Snow Days party of the season' (article 1953, confirmed by lookup). problems.issue: Dec 9 is a reconstructed bound (R) resting on one party date. The only sourced run is Dec 18, 2009 to Jan 3, 2010. The (R) label and reason are present, but the reason is weak.
problems.fix: Either use the sourced Dec 18 start, or keep Dec 9 and state it as a lower-confidence (R) bound that covers the 2010 party. Do not present it as a sourced run start.

problems.issue: Jan 3 is sourced only for 2009-10. The later-year ends are assumed, and 2010 and 2011 have null ends. The (R) flag is present.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) flag. A builder should not treat Jan 3 as a verified end for 2010 or 2011.

problems.issue: The evidence pack says the UK/Europe session was 'Fri Dec 10, 2010 9am Pacific / 4pm GMT'. In December, Pacific is UTC-8, so 9am Pacific is 5pm GMT, not 4pm. The conversion is wrong, though the answer does not use it in the row.
problems.fix: Correct to 5pm GMT or drop the GMT figure.

problems.issue: I could not re-find article 892 ('over until next year') or the 'annual' wording in 2429/2808 with lookup. They rest on the pack's summaries. The 2009-10 and 2010 sources check out.
problems.fix: Re-read 892 and 2429 before relying on 'annual' for the yearly recurrence.

critiques.notes: Verified with lookup: articles 705, 709, 718 give a daily Snow Days run Dec 18, 2009 to Jan 3, 2010. The calendar is sound apart from the reconstructed start. The yearly recurrence is reasonable for a holiday season, and no slots are invented. Halloween does not overlap Dec-Jan. The wrap-year scheduler support is unconfirmed, and the answer already flags it. Wireable: yes, as a provisional Dec 18 (sourced) to Jan 3 (2009-10) window, or Dec 9 (R) to Jan 3 (R) if the builder accepts reconstruction.

problems.issue: Dec 9 is a reconstructed (R) lower bound taken from the 2010 'first Snow Days party' date (article 1953). problems.fix: Keep Dec 9 only as a flagged (R) window, or set the sourced start to Dec 18 and note that 2010 may have opened earlier. Do not present Dec 9 as the opening date in original_dates.

problems.issue: Jan 3 is sourced only for 2009-10. The wiki says the event runs 'December throughout January', so a Jan 3 end may cut off later runs. The 2010 and 2011 end dates are null and the end is assumed for later years.

problems.issue: The start field reads as a confirmed season start, but the source text describes only a community party 'first of the season' and says the season start is not confirmed. The field and its note disagree.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks out for the sourced 2009-10 run (Dec 18, 2009 to Jan 3, 2010 confirmed in articles 705, 709, 718). critiques.notes: Verified in articles.json:17507-17526 and the fact:event rows: both articles 640 and 641 are titled 'Evento Comunitario: Reto JCC', both have null dates, both describe a weekly PvP JCC event meeting at Encrucijada or the JCC lobby with NPC Mar Mita, and 641 says it ran on Friday 20 November in two blocks on Server 1. Yearly recurrence is supported by 'annual' wording in undated articles and by the wiki; the 2011 run is wiki-only. Later years are unconfirmed.
Live status is unsure: no source after 2011-06-04 confirms the event runs now. Do not wire until a dated article or staff confirmation is found.
Joyful Valley (article 976) and Vegalegre (article 2018) are localized zone names; Merry Vale is the English zone.
Stone Heart's Rampage timing and the 15-minute spawn rule are wiki-only and unsourced; no slot cadence is set.
No announcement text or locale id for a pre-event notice was found; announce is null.
Item prices and currencies are unknown; SC Marketplace categories are inferred, not priced.
Quest titles are not confirmed in the client; the daily and members-only quests are listed generically.
The PS3 launch post is undated and is a platform note for the same run, not a separate occurrence.
The answer pack's title named the villain (Stone Heart); the event is the Festival of Hearts.

problems.issue: The only dated entry (2010-02-12 to 2010-02-12) is the community semi-formal dance on Friday 12 Feb 2010 (articles 960, 957). The row's own open note says it dates the dance only, not the festival run. Putting it in original_dates as the occurrence start/end presents a one-evening dance as the event's 2010 window.
problems.fix: Remove it from original_dates, or record it as a sub-activity dated 2010-02-12 with a note. Leave the 2010 festival occurrence with no start/end until a source gives one.

problems.issue: The wiki intro says 'from February through March', which supports months only. The day bounds 1 Feb and 31 Mar are chosen, not sourced. The (R) marker is present, but the source field reads like a dated window.
problems.fix: Keep the months as the sourced part. Mark the day bounds as a reconstruction with the reason 'month-level wiki wording only; no dated article'. Do not present the window as a sourced season.

problems.issue: 'Yearly' rests on undated 'annual' wording (articles 969, 2016, 2500, 2501, wiki) and on the wiki's 'annual' sentence. No dated article confirms any year after the 2010 dance, and the 2011 run is wiki-only pet text (wiki:Cupid, wiki:Heart Critter). The recurrence is plausible but its evidence is thinner than the row implies.
problems.fix: State that yearly recurrence is inferred from 'annual' wording in undated posts. Record 2011 as wiki-only. Do not treat later years as confirmed.

problems.issue: Stone Heart's Rampage is sourced only by the quest objective text (locale:427178), which confirms the rampage exists but not its timing. The row lists it as an activity without a cadence. That is acceptable only because the row marks the timing as unsourced.
problems.fix: Keep it as an unscheduled activity. Do not add any clock time or interval.

problems.issue: Merry Vale is supported by the English articles and locale, and by video frames showing Merry Vale. Joyful Valley (976) and Vegalegre (2018) are localized names. The row handles this correctly and the zone list is fine.
problems.fix: None required.

critiques.notes: Verified: articles 960, 969, 1009, 2016, 2498, 2499, 2500, 2501, 2522 and 2018 exist and say what the row claims. Wiki pages for Heart Breakers, Dove, Cupid, Heart Critter, Hearts Outfit and the SC Marketplace items exist with the stated wording. The 'Feb through March' sentence is in the wiki intro. The row is honest about its gaps: the festival's own start and end, live status, and prices are all open. The main failure is that the 2010 dance date is filed as the occurrence window in original_dates, and the Feb 1 and Mar 31 day bounds are a choice presented in a season field. Not wireable: no dated source gives the festival window and live status is unknown.

problems.issue: The 1 Feb to 31 Mar window is taken from one wiki sentence ('February through March'). The pack missed a dated 2010 article that gives a shorter run. The Feb 8, 2010 SOE press release (articles.json ~line 11604) calls the Festival of Hearts a 'month-long' event. A two-month window therefore swallows roughly a month of unrelated time, and the evidence for it is weaker than the answer claims.
problems.fix: Keep the Feb start as (R) but mark the end as unconfirmed. Cite the 'month-long' press release as the duration source, and either bound the window to about 30 days from the 2010 start or hold the season until a dated end is found.

problems.issue: The answer says the Feb 12, 2010 item 'dates the dance only' and that the festival's own 2010 window is not stated. The Feb 12, 2010 update notes (articles.json ~line 11674) announce the Festival of Hearts event in Merry Vale, with a daily prize wheel, coin wheel and member benefits. That is a festival-run date, not only a dance date. The answer's 'dance only' reading is wrong, and the 2010 start should be taken from this source.
problems.fix: Set the 2010 occurrence start to 2010-02-12 (from the update notes, articles 960/957 area) and cite it as the festival launch, with the dance noted as a sub-event. Keep end unknown unless the month-long figure is used as a (R) bound.

problems.issue: 'yearly_season' rests on undated 'annual' wording in articles 969, 2016, 2500, 2501 and on the wiki. The Spanish and French returns (articles 16574, 16588, 16630) are also undated. Only the 2010 run is dated, so yearly recurrence is plausible but not shown for any later year that a builder could check.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season but state that only 2010 is dated and that later years rest on undated 'returns' posts. Do not claim a yearly cadence is confirmed.

problems.issue: The answer says 'no article after 2011-06-04' but does not check the dated 2012 wiki news ('Update of February 7, 2012', Festival of Hearts in Merry Vale) found in the wiki news archive. That is a 2012 run that would widen the set of years and bear on the yearly claim.
problems.fix: Add the Feb 7, 2012 update to original_dates as a second occurrence, or explain why it is excluded.

problems.issue: Zone and NPC naming is mixed: 'Joyful Valley' (French) and 'Vegalegre' (Spanish) are treated as localized names, but the French post also names a different pixie pair (Valentin and Arianna). That is a legend variant and is not noted.
problems.fix: Note the Valentin/Rylan name variant as a localization detail in notes; it does not change the dates.

critiques.notes: The event identity (Festival of Hearts, Merry Vale, annual, Feb 2010 start) is sound. The calendar is not: the season window rests on a single wiki sentence while a 2010 press release gives a month-long run, and the 2010 occurrence is treated as dance-only when the Feb 12, 2010 update announced the festival itself. Fix the window and the 2010 start before any wiring. The row is not wireable as it stands.

problems.issue: The 2010 entry sets start and end to 2010-02-12, the single-day community semi-formal dance (articles 957, 960). The row's own source says it dates the dance only, not the festival run. As written, the field reads as the festival's 2010 run, which no source supports.
problems.fix: Either drop this entry from original_dates and keep the dance as a separate community-event note, or mark it as a dance with start=end=2010-02-12 and state in the record that it is not the festival window. Record the 2010 festival window as unknown.

problems.issue: The only source is the wiki intro sentence 'held from February through March'. It gives months, not days. Day bounds are an invented choice, even though marked (R). The row also cites the wiki as the sole basis for the window.
problems.fix: Keep the months as the sourced window and state that the day bounds are unsourced placeholders. Do not present 1 Feb and 31 Mar as dated facts. A builder should not treat this as a confirmed window.

problems.issue: Yearly recurrence rests on 'annual' wording in undated articles (969, 2016, 2500, 2501) and on the wiki. Only one dated occurrence (the dance, 2010) exists, and the 2011 run is wiki-only. The cadence is plausible but not established by a dated source for the festival itself.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season as a hypothesis, flagged as resting on undated 'annual' wording. Do not claim a recurrence confirmed by dates.

problems.issue: The 2010 year for the festival is inferred from article 976's relative timing ('about 1 year 3 months' before capture). That is an inference from a vague relative phrase, not a stated date, and the row mentions it only in open items.
problems.fix: Label the 2010 festival occurrence as inferred in the record itself, not only in open, or drop it until a dated source is found.

problems.issue: No source after 2011-06-04 shows the event running now, and the window is a placeholder. The row correctly says not wireable, which matches the evidence.
problems.fix: Keep wireable false until a dated article or staff confirmation gives the festival's own window.

critiques.notes: Most listed evidence checks out: the wiki intro, the locale strings (4452, 5518, 400038, 426989, 427176, 427178), and articles 969, 1009, 2016, 2498, 2499, 2500, 2501 and 2522 all exist as described. The row is honest about its gaps in open, and the zone, NPC and reward claims are sourced. The failure is structural: original_dates presents a one-day dance as the festival's 2010 run, and the season day bounds are not sourced. Fix those and the row is a fair partial record, still not wireable.

problems.issue: The only dated occurrence is the 12 Feb 2010 community dance (articles 957, 960), but it is recorded as the festival run with start = end = 2010-02-12. The answer's own open list says the dance is not the festival run. A scheduler reading this would treat the festival as a one-day event in 2010, which contradicts the Feb to Mar season window.
problems.fix: Remove this entry from original_dates, or record it as a separate 'community_dance' occurrence with a note that it does not bound the festival. Leave original_dates empty (or mark the 2010 festival window as unknown) until a dated article gives the run.

problems.issue: The 1 Feb and 31 Mar day bounds are a (R) choice from the wiki phrase 'February through March'. The wiki gives months only and the Valentine's date (14 Feb) is not used as an anchor. The window is sourced at month level only.
problems.fix: Keep the month window as a wiki-sourced placeholder, but state in the source field that only the months are sourced and the day bounds are reconstructed, with the reason. Do not present the day bounds as dated.

problems.issue: 'yearly_season' is a sensible kind for a Valentine's holiday, but the yearly claim rests on undated 'annual' wording and on wiki-only 2011 pet pages. Only the 2010 dance is dated, and it does not show the festival repeating.
problems.fix: Keep yearly_season as the intended cadence, but note that recurrence is unconfirmed past 2010 and that live status is unknown.

problems.issue: The season window has a wiki sentence as its source, so a builder could load it as a placeholder. However the window is unconfirmed by any dated article, live status is 'unsure', and the 2010 occurrence is wrong.
problems.fix: Keep wireable false until a dated article gives the festival's own start and end, and the row's original_dates is corrected.

critiques.notes: The season is not a clash: no Festival of Hearts season exists, and Feb to Mar does not swallow Halloween (Sep 20 to Nov 11). The name reuse is fine. The main calendar defect is that the dance date is being used as the festival's occurrence. The row's own open list already admits this, so the answer contradicts itself. The evidence lens is out of scope here, but the 2011 wiki-only run and the undated 'annual' posts are correctly flagged as unconfirmed.

Darkthorne and Queen Valerian are plot figures with no client NPC record cited, so npcs is empty.
Zones, quests and clock times are unsourced. The Halloween season is not reused here because this promotion has no sourced window.

problems.issue: The row gives no date and live='unsure', which is honest, but it misses dated facts that are in the pack and that bound the promotion. Cover #1 of the print comic is marked 'SEP 09' (wiki image FreeRealmsComicCover1.jpg), and the Spelunker's Shard wiki page says the Facebook Treasure Trader also gave that item until the app was discontinued on September 28, 2010. The row cites neither. The answer also says 'no dated source' when the pack has at least a 2009 print date and a 2010 end bound for a related channel.
problems.fix: Record the sourced bounds as facts with their sources: print comic #1 SEP 09 (cover), and the Facebook app discontinued 2010-09-28 (wiki, Spelunker's Shard). Mark the code-redemption window itself as unknown, and state that the bounds are not the window.

problems.issue: The claim 'each of the 12 issues carries a unique code' rests on an undated article. That supports the mechanic, not any window. This is correctly flagged in open, but the row's confidence of 0.2 and the 'one_off_replay' recurrence rest on the mechanic alone.
problems.fix: Keep the mechanic as sourced and label the window as unknown. Do not give a recurrence until a dated source is found.

problems.issue: 'one_off_replay' with 'fixed set of redeemable items, with no date gating' is a design choice, not a sourced fact. The evidence does not show that codes were ever un-gated or that they were date-limited.

problems.issue: Only the code-to-item links for #9 and #10 are listed, and they come from wiki pages. The Spelunker's Shard link is the one with the Facebook end date, so it is the best-sourced item. The Flute link is wiki-only and is labelled that way. This is acceptable, but the claim 'Spelunker's Shard (comic #9 code)' is not confirmed against a dated article, as the row admits.
problems.fix: Keep both items labelled as wiki-only. Note that the Facebook end date applies to the app's random drop, not to the code.

critiques.notes: The mechanic (12 issues, a unique in-game code per issue) is sourced to articleId=936 and the wiki. Client item names 5513 and 6957 exist. problems.fix: Keep original_dates empty for the code window. Add a calendar_facts or open note listing the print-series bounds (2009-07-29 issue #1 on sale, SEP 09 cover, 2010 cover for #10), each marked as print-only, not code-redemption dates.

Furniture (Bed, Sofa, Chair, Dining Table, Floor Lamp, Wall Sconce, Furniture Bundle) is dated to 2012 only by the wiki Template:News/Archive (April 24, 2012 update), not by article 2580. Bundle price locale:692 (1350 Station Cash) does not name the bundle, so no price is paired.
Four pinata pet names, prices and currency are unknown.
Party-prep NPC lines (locale 428071, 428550, 428708, 428710, 428711, 428726, 432476; Glerga, Sal Monella, Quills, Bordon Cloo) name the Bash but carry no year; excluded from dated facts.

'Birthday Bash' is generic. Earlier birthday articles (1197, 1261, 1282, 2106, 2107) are other years and not attached. locale:19968 'Making this Birthday Bash a Summer Splash' belongs to the Seaside Summer Splash and is excluded.
Halloween season (09-20..11-11) does not overlap any candidate window, so no name reuse applies.
Announcement text not sourced; announce is null.

problems.issue: The 2012 start is the announcement date (04-26), not a run start. Article 2580 confirms only the end (through May 24, 2012) and the name. I could not confirm the 2026-04-26 announcement date from lookup either. A window starting on an announcement date is a stand-in, not evidence of when the Bash ran. The (R) flag is present, but the start is still presented as a season date.
problems.fix: Either keep the start as an explicit (R) anchor on the wiki's April 29 anniversary (wiki Category:Birthday Bash Weapons says the event is tied to April 29), or mark the start as unknown and carry only end=05-24 with the announcement as a note. State the choice in the source field.

problems.issue: The source text says the 2013 run 'could not be re-confirmed by lookup'. Lookup now confirms article 2924 as SOE's post for the 4th birthday on April 29, 2013, with the Ambassadors and a Birthday Bash area in Sanctuary. The 2013 start is supported; only the end is missing. The pack's caveat is stale.
problems.fix: Update the 2013 entry to cite article 2924 as confirmed for the April 29, 2013 start. Leave end null and say so.

problems.issue: Yearly season is reasonable, but it rests on two years with one fully dated end (2012) and one partly dated start (2013). 'Free Realms Turns Three!' (locale:706) was not checked in this pass, though locale:707 (Camellia, Cakenstein) is confirmed. The pinata-pet line and the Marketplace furniture are wiki or article-only items and are correctly marked as such.
problems.fix: Keep the quest as partly confirmed (locale:707 confirmed, title locale:706 unchecked). Keep the furniture and pinata items under open.

critiques.notes: Confirmed by lookup: article 2580 (2012 third-anniversary Bash, ran through May 24, 2012; Queen Valerian cake bake-off in Sanctuary; daily party-prep quests; Cakenstein in Sacred Grove; login for the free Birthday Cake hat). Article 2924 (4th birthday on April 29, 2013; Ambassadors; Birthday Bash area in Sanctuary). Locale 695 (2012 3rd anniversary), 707 (Camellia and Cakenstein), and the furniture names 666, 436980-436983, 437014, 691 exist as stated. The wiki's 'annual April event tied to April 29' is a general statement and is fine as a recurrence hint. The main evidence gap is the 2012 start date. Wireable is true only as a 2012-end-anchored, (R)-flagged season; a builder should not treat 04-26 as a sourced opening.

problems.issue: The 04-29 start is not dated to any single year that also has the 05-24 end. It comes from the 2013 post (article 2924, 'Free Realms' 4th birthday on April 29 (2013)'), while the end comes from 2012 (article 2580, 'ran through May 24, 2012'). The combined 04-29..05-24 window is therefore a cross-year reconstruction. The (R) note admits this, but the window is still presented as the season.
problems.fix: Keep the window marked (R) with the reason that start and end come from different years, or split the record into a per-year anniversary anchor (04-29) plus a run length that is unknown. Do not present 04-29..05-24 as a sourced season.

problems.issue: The wiki says the event is an annual April event, but the only sourced end (May 24, 2012) falls in May. The yearly_season recurrence therefore assumes an April-to-May window that no source confirms for 2014+.
problems.fix: Record the disagreement explicitly. Set recurrence to a yearly anchor on April 29 with an open run length, or mark it admin_only until a later year is dated.

problems.issue: 2012 start is null, so the only 2012 date is an end date. A builder cannot use the 2012 row as a range, and the 2013 row has no end. Neither row alone gives a full run.
problems.fix: Leave both rows as partial, and flag the season as not fully dated per year in the schema, or drop the season window until a year has both ends.

problems.issue: 'Birthday Bash' is generic. The pack notes earlier birthday articles (1197, 1261, 1282, 2106, 2107) and a locale string 'Making this Birthday Bash a Summer Splash' (locale 2642737684) that suggests a different, summer-extended year. A season window of 04-29..05-24 would not cover that, and a yearly season could swallow unrelated birthday items.
problems.fix: Note the Summer Splash variant as a separate or unresolved year, and restrict the season to the dated 2012 and 2013 anniversary runs.

problems.issue: No existing season is reused, which is correct. Halloween (09-20..11-11) does not overlap, so there is no collision.
problems.fix: None needed.

critiques.notes: The 2013 start (04-29) and 2012 end (05-24) check out against the articles summaries. The 2012 start and the 04-29 season window remain reconstructions across years. The row is wireable only as a flagged (R) window, not as a sourced calendar season. Halloween has no conflict.

problems.issue: The 2013 start of 2013-04-29 is the date of the SOE 4th-birthday post (article 2924, 'Free Realms' 4th birthday on April 29 (2013)'). The lookup summary says the post invites players to the Birthday Bash area, but it does not say the Bash started that day. Recording the post date as the run start is an unsupported claim.
problems.fix: Set the 2013 start to null with a note that the post is dated 2013-04-29, or mark it as (R) anniversary anchor. Do not present it as a sourced opening date.

problems.issue: The 04-29 start is an (R) anchor taken from the anniversary date, not a sourced opening. The 2012 run start is unknown and the announcement was 04-26. The window is stitched from two different years (2012 end, 2013 post date), so no single year is dated on both ends.
problems.fix: Keep the (R) label but say explicitly that the start is the launch anniversary and not a verified opening. Consider making the season window admin-confirmed before scheduling.

problems.issue: End 05-24 comes from one year (2012) and the run length is therefore a single data point. The article says the Bash 'ran through May 24, 2012', which supports the end only for 2012.
problems.fix: Label the end as 2012-only and leave the run length open for 2013 and later.

problems.issue: 'yearly_season' rests on the wiki's general 'annual April' statement, which I could not verify against a dated source. Two data points (2012 May end, 2013 April post) do not establish a yearly cadence for 2014+.
problems.fix: Use 'admin_only' or mark the cadence as an unverified recommendation until a 2014 or later occurrence is dated.

problems.issue: Wiki-only furniture dates (Template:News/Archive, April 24, 2012) are used in dated runs and the 2012 year. The article does not confirm them. This is flagged in open, but the 'runs' list still includes the wiki furniture as a 2012 prop.
problems.fix: Move wiki-only furniture out of the dated runs list or tag it as unconfirmed in runs.

critiques.notes: Verified with lookup: article 2580 gives the 2012 third-anniversary Bash running through May 24, 2012, with the Queen Valerian cake bake-off, daily prep quests, Cakenstein and a Birthday Cake hat login reward. Article 2924 is a 4th-birthday post dated April 29, 2013 inviting players to the Ambassadors and the Birthday Bash area in Sanctuary, with no rewards and no run dates. Locale checks confirm 695 (3rd anniversary), 706/707 (Turns Three quest and Camellia/Cakenstein dialog), and furniture names 436980-437014 and 666. Party-prep NPC lines (428071 etc.) carry no year and are correctly excluded from dated facts. The answer is honest about its gaps (open list is thorough), but original_dates treats a post date as a run start, which fails the evidence lens. The row is wireable only as a clearly marked (R) window, not as a sourced schedule.

problems.issue: The wiki Birthday Bash page says the event is held 'throughout the month of April' and ties it to April 29. The 2012 run instead ends May 24, which the answer already flags. The answer does not record this conflict in the calendar fields, and the 'yearly April anchor' rests on that general statement.
problems.fix: Record the wiki 'throughout April' statement next to the 2012 May 24 end as a source conflict. Keep the yearly window as unresolved until a 2014+ run or a second source confirms the span.

problems.issue: The 2012 announcement date (2012-04-26) in the evidence pack is not carried into original_dates, so the only 2012 bound is an end date with no start.
problems.fix: Add the announcement date as a non-run field (for example announced: 2012-04-26) so the row keeps the one dated 2012 fact that exists.

problems.issue: season is null and the candidate 04-29..05-24 window is reconstructed across years with no 2014+ confirmation. That is correctly kept out of season.
problems.fix: No change needed now. Keep admin_only until a sourced window exists.

critiques.notes: Checked the article 2580 summary: third-anniversary Bash 'ran through May 24, 2012', with the cake bake-off, party-prep quests and Cakenstein. Wiki Birthday Bash page confirms 'annual event held throughout the month of April' for the April 29 launch anniversary. Halloween (09-20..11-11) does not overlap, so no name reuse. admin_only recurrence is sensible for an event with no sourced yearly run. The row is honest about what is missing. It is not wireable as a season or slot cadence, so staff must start it by hand.

revival.why: A dated Marketplace discount with no source showing it recurs on a calendar or slot. Staff should start and stop it manually for the revival's store. It is not a yearly season (no season window is evidenced) and not a repeating slot. Members-only sales (May 25-28, 2012) and other weekend sales are separate events and are not merged here.

evidence.claim: Official post: up to 30% off Station Cash items in the Marketplace, memberships excluded, valid 12:01AM PDT 8/10/2012 to 11:59PM PDT 8/12/2012
Spanish article: 30% off Station Cash items in the Marketplace during August 10 to 12, 2012
Spanish article: 30% off Station Cash items, three days, 12:01 AM PDT 8/10/2012 to 11:59 PM PDT 8/12/2012
In-game UI title 'Weekend Price Cuts' (locale:862) and banner 'Everything in the Marketplace is 30% off!' (locale:863); re-checked this session via lookup
Video frame banner 'Weekend Price Cuts / Everything in the Marketplace is 30% off! / Time Left: 2 Days' (live in client; date not shown)

open: Only one dated occurrence (Aug 10-12, 2012). No source says it was the first, and it is not shown to recur, so no recurrence is set beyond admin_only.
Article texts for 2707/2712/2716 were not re-read this session (article lookups returned errors); dates rely on the prior pass's quoted offer text and fact lines.
articleId=2700 (Portuguese, Marketplace weekend sale up to 30% off) is undated and may be the same or a separate sale; needs a direct read.
No items, prices or currency are tied to this sale by any source; the item fields are left empty.
Article 2707 posted date (2012-08-10) is inferred from a relative stamp; the offer window is the quoted one.
The pack's merged 'Weekend Sale' label covers separate events (members-only sales 2609/2611 on May 25-28, 2012, President's Day housing sale 2528, TCG booster weekend sales). None are counted here.

problems.issue: The Aug 10-12, 2012 window is supported. The articles facts index has the 2707 offer line ("Get up to 30% off Station Cash items in the Marketplace! Hurry, ends 8/12/12!", duration 3 days), the 2712 line ("Oferta valida de las 12:01AM PDT 8/10/2012 hasta las 11:59PM PDT 8/12/2012"), and the 2716 fact ("from 12:01 AM PDT on 8/10/2012 to 11:59 PM PDT on 8/12/2012"). The 2707 posted date of 2012-08-10 is only inferred, and the answer already says so.
problems.fix: No change needed to the window. Keep the 'posted date inferred' caveat.

problems.issue: Locale 862 and 863 resolve to the strings quoted. But the locale table shows text only, not that it was live in 2012. Liveness rests on the video frames (00040, 00082, 00102), which show the banner but no date.
problems.fix: Keep 'live: yes' but state that the 2012 date rests on the official posts, and that the video frames only show the banner is present in the client.

problems.issue: The Portuguese article 2700 is titled "Vem aí - Liquidação do Fim de Semana!" ('coming soon: weekend sale'), with date null. It may be the announcement of this same sale or a different weekend sale. It is not dated, yet the answer leaves it as an open item and does not use it.
problems.fix: Read article 2700 directly and either add it as a corroborating source for Aug 2012 or record it as a separate sale.

problems.issue: The row has one dated occurrence, no season window and no slot cadence. The wireable test asks for a season window or slot cadence with sources, and neither exists, so the row cannot be loaded as a recurring entry. The admin_only setting is consistent with the evidence.
problems.fix: Mark as a one-off dated promotion (2012-08-10 to 2012-08-12) that staff start and stop manually. Do not present it as a schedulable season or slot.

problems.issue: The source facts attach locale_id 30149 and 385941 to lines whose quotes are Spanish article text (from 2712/2716), and the Station Cash fact at 2716 reuses the 2712 quote. These are mismatched citations that a reviewer could confuse.
problems.fix: Cite the quote and article for each fact line individually; drop the locale ids from the 2716 fact unless a locale string is verified to say this.

critiques.notes: The core claim (30% off Station Cash items in the Marketplace, memberships/subscriptions excluded, Aug 10-12, 2012, PDT window) is supported by several articles and by the in-game banner. The answer correctly leaves out the May members-only sale and other weekend sales. The main gap is that the row is a single dated occurrence with no cadence, so it is a valid record but not wireable by the scheduler. Article 2700 should be read before the evidence is called complete.

problems.issue: The announce text 'Everything in the Marketplace is 30% off!' (locale:863) overstates the sale. Every dated source (articleId 2707, 2712, 2716, fact lines) limits the 30% off to Station Cash items in the Marketplace, memberships excluded. The row's own activities field says this correctly, so the announce text contradicts the row.
problems.fix: Keep locale 863 as the in-game banner text if you like, but label it as the banner and state in the row that the discount covers Station Cash items only (memberships excluded). Do not use it as the scope of the sale.

problems.issue: The single 2012-08-10 to 2012-08-12 window is well sourced. I confirmed it in the articles index: 2707 says 'Hurry, ends 8/12/12!', 2712 says 'August 10 to 12, 2012', and 2716 gives 12:01 AM PDT 8/10/2012 to 11:59 PM PDT 8/12/2012. The 2700 Portuguese article is still undated, so it cannot yet rule out a second sale in another window. The open list handles this correctly.
problems.fix: No change to the dates. Read article 2700 directly before treating 2012-08 as the only occurrence.

problems.issue: admin_only is the right call. No source shows a season, a yearly repeat or a slot. The sale is not merged with the May 25-28 members-only sale or the Feb 17-20 housing sale, which keeps the window from swallowing unrelated months. Season stays null, which is correct: the Halloween season in seasons_already_defined is unrelated.
problems.fix: None.

critiques.notes: Calendar checks: the dates agree across the three articles, and the window is one occurrence with no cross-year claim, so there is no year conflict. The row is loadable as a one-off dated window with admin_only recurrence. The main defect is the announce text, which states a broader scope than the sources support. Confidence 0.6 is reasonable given the single occurrence and the undated 2700 article.
